cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) says unto him, See you tell no man; but go your way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.
cards.tgt_text: And when he saw them, he said unto them, Go shew yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed.
cards.old_note: The second leper-episode in Luke; Yahusha (Jesus) again sends the cleansed to the priest.
cards.note: Luke 17:14 — *And when he saw them, he said unto them, Go shew yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed.* *And Yahusha (Jesus) says unto him, See you tell no man; but go your way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.* (Matthew 8:4) In Matthew the man is healed and then told to *shew thyself to the priest*. Here ten men hear nearly the same word, *Go shew yourselves unto the priests*, and are cleansed *as they went*. Yahusha (Jesus) heals them, and then he sends them down the road Moses laid out.
cards.prose: In Matthew the man is healed and then told to *shew thyself to the priest*. Here ten men hear nearly the same word, *Go shew yourselves unto the priests*, and are cleansed *as they went*. Yahusha (Jesus) heals them, and then he sends them down the road Moses laid out.
cards.member_note: Luke 17:14 — *And when he saw them, he said unto them, Go shew yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed.* Ten lepers are sent to the priests as Moses laid down and are cleansed on the way, the same road the healed man in Matthew takes.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) says unto him, See you tell no man; but go your way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.
cards.tgt_text: Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.
cards.old_note: The Torah-affirming Sermon-on-the-Mount declaration the first-miracle illustrates in practice.
cards.note: Matthew 5:17 — *Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.* *And Yahusha (Jesus) says unto him, See you tell no man; but go your way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.* (Matthew 8:4) He said he had not come to destroy the law or the prophets, and here is the first healing after the Sermon. He touches the leper, and then sends him to the priest with *the gift that Moses commanded*. The word on the mountain and the word to the leper are one word.
cards.prose: He said he had not come to destroy the law or the prophets, and here is the first healing after the Sermon. He touches the leper, and then sends him to the priest with *the gift that Moses commanded*. The word on the mountain and the word to the leper are one word.
cards.member_note: Matthew 5:17 — *Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.* He says plainly that he has not come to destroy the law or the prophets, which the sending of the leper to the priest bears out.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) says unto him, See you tell no man; but go your way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.
cards.tgt_text: And when he was departed thence, he went into their synagogue:
cards.old_note: The Shabbat-healing of the man with the withered hand — same heart-Torah-walking-in-practice pattern; the oral-tradition Shabbat-fence broken; the Torah's mercy-substance preserved.
cards.note: Matthew 12:9 — *And when he was departed thence, he went into their synagogue:* *And Yahusha (Jesus) says unto him, See you tell no man; but go your way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.* (Matthew 8:4) Here he sends a healed man to the priest with the gift Moses commanded, and there he walks into *their synagogue* on the Sabbath, where men are waiting to accuse him. His answer, *it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days* (Matthew 12:12), is the same Torah kept in both places, against what had been laid over it.
cards.prose: Here he sends a healed man to the priest with the gift Moses commanded, and there he walks into *their synagogue* on the Sabbath, where men are waiting to accuse him. His answer, *it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days* (Matthew 12:12), is the same Torah kept in both places, against what had been laid over it.
cards.member_note: Matthew 12:9 — *And when he was departed thence, he went into their synagogue:* He enters the synagogue where the man with the withered hand is waiting, and what follows is the Torah kept against the rules laid over it.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) says unto him, See you tell no man; but go your way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.
cards.tgt_text: For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:
cards.old_note: Yahusha's (Jesus's) explicit distinction between the Torah of Elohim (God) and the *tradition of men;* the heart-Torah affirmed, the oral-tradition distortions corrected.
cards.note: Mark 7:10 — *For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:* *And Yahusha (Jesus) says unto him, See you tell no man; but go your way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.* (Matthew 8:4) In Matthew the gift is the one *Moses commanded*, and he sends the man to give it. In Mark the elders hold up another gift, Corban, as a reason for a man to do nothing for his father or mother. He stands with what Moses said and sets their tradition aside.
cards.prose: In Matthew the gift is the one *Moses commanded*, and he sends the man to give it. In Mark the elders hold up another gift, Corban, as a reason for a man to do nothing for his father or mother. He stands with what Moses said and sets their tradition aside.
cards.member_note: Mark 7:10 — *For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:* Moses said to honour father and mother, and Yahusha (Jesus) holds to that commandment against the tradition that emptied it.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) says unto him, See you tell no man; but go your way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.
cards.tgt_text: And the word of Elohim (God) increased; and the number of the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem greatly; and a great company of the priests were obedient to the faith.
cards.old_note: *A great company of the priests were obedient to the faith* — the eventual response of some priests to the testimony the leper-cleansings constituted.
cards.note: Acts 6:7 — *And the word of Elohim (God) increased; and the number of the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem greatly; and a great company of the priests were obedient to the faith.* *And Yahusha (Jesus) says unto him, See you tell no man; but go your way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.* (Matthew 8:4) He told the cleansed man to go to the priest *for a testimony unto them*. Some time later, in Jerusalem, *a great company of the priests* are obedient. The testimony that began with a leper carrying his offering to the priest did reach the priesthood.
cards.prose: He told the cleansed man to go to the priest *for a testimony unto them*. Some time later, in Jerusalem, *a great company of the priests* are obedient. The testimony that began with a leper carrying his offering to the priest did reach the priesthood.
cards.member_note: Acts 6:7 — *And the word of Elohim (God) increased; and the number of the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem greatly; and a great company of the priests were obedient to the faith.* A great company of the priests become obedient in Jerusalem, so the testimony the cleansed were sent to give the priesthood was heard.

cards.src_text: When he was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.
cards.tgt_text: And the leper in whom the plague is, his clothes shall be rent, and his head bare, and he shall put a covering upon his upper lip, and shall cry, Unclean, unclean.
cards.old_note: The leper's required posture under the Torah's purity-architecture; the defiling-condition Yahusha's (Jesus's) touch reverses.
cards.note: Leviticus 13:45 — *And the leper in whom the plague is, his clothes shall be rent, and his head bare, and he shall put a covering upon his upper lip, and shall cry, Unclean, unclean.* *When he was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.* (Matthew 8:1) Great crowds follow him down from the mountain, and the first to meet him is a man the Torah required to cry *Unclean, unclean*. The Torah shut him outside, and Yahusha (Jesus) puts out his hand and touches him, then sends him back in through the same Torah, to the priest.
cards.prose: Great crowds follow him down from the mountain, and the first to meet him is a man the Torah required to cry *Unclean, unclean*. The Torah shut him outside, and Yahusha (Jesus) puts out his hand and touches him, then sends him back in through the same Torah, to the priest.
cards.member_note: Leviticus 13:45 — *And the leper in whom the plague is, his clothes shall be rent, and his head bare, and he shall put a covering upon his upper lip, and shall cry, Unclean, unclean.* This shows the place the Torah gave the leper, outside and crying unclean, which the touch of Yahusha (Jesus) lifts.

cards.src_text: When he was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.
cards.tgt_text: And it came to pass, as he went to Jerusalem, that he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.
cards.old_note: The second-leper episode; Yahusha (Jesus) again directs the cleansed (ten lepers) to *go shew yourselves unto the priests* — same Torah-procedure affirmation.
cards.note: Luke 17:11 — *And it came to pass, as he went to Jerusalem, that he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.* *When he was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.* (Matthew 8:1) Luke puts him on the road *through the midst of Samaria and Galilee*, and the ten lepers who meet him there get the same word as the man in Matthew: *Go shew yourselves unto the priests* (Luke 17:14). Wherever the road runs, the way back for a leper runs through the priest.
cards.prose: Luke puts him on the road *through the midst of Samaria and Galilee*, and the ten lepers who meet him there get the same word as the man in Matthew: *Go shew yourselves unto the priests* (Luke 17:14). Wherever the road runs, the way back for a leper runs through the priest.
cards.member_note: Luke 17:11 — *And it came to pass, as he went to Jerusalem, that he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.* Luke sets the road through Samaria and Galilee where ten lepers meet him and are sent to the priests, the same procedure as in Matthew.

cards.src_text: And when Yahusha (Jesus) was entered into Capernaum, there came unto him a centurion, beseeching him,
cards.tgt_text: Now when he had ended all his sayings in the audience of the people, he entered into Capernaum.
cards.old_note: The Lukan parallel with the additional detail of the Jewish-elders' intercession and the centurion's standing in the Kfar-Nachum (Capernaum) gathering.
cards.note: Luke 7:1 — *Now when he had ended all his sayings in the audience of the people, he entered into Capernaum.* *And when Yahusha (Jesus) was entered into Capernaum, there came unto him a centurion, beseeching him,* (Matthew 8:5) Luke opens the same scene in Capernaum, and what he adds is that the centurion did not come first himself. He sent the elders of the Yahudim (Jews) to speak for him, so the man who comes *beseeching him* in Matthew has already been vouched for.
cards.prose: Luke opens the same scene in Capernaum, and what he adds is that the centurion did not come first himself. He sent the elders of the Yahudim (Jews) to speak for him, so the man who comes *beseeching him* in Matthew has already been vouched for.
cards.member_note: Luke 7:1 — *Now when he had ended all his sayings in the audience of the people, he entered into Capernaum.* Luke brings him into Capernaum and tells that the centurion first sent elders of the Yahudim (Jews) to ask on his behalf.

cards.src_text: And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.
cards.tgt_text: Behold, I will bring them from the north country, and gather them from the coasts of the earth, and with them the blind and the lame, the woman with child and her that travaileth with child together: a great company shall return thither.
cards.old_note: The Yirmeyahu (Jeremiah) 31 gathering-prophecy chapter Matthew has been weaving through the gospel since Matt 2:18.
cards.note: Jeremiah 31:8 — *Behold, I will bring them from the north country, and gather them from the coasts of the earth, and with them the blind and the lame, the woman with child and her that travaileth with child together: a great company shall return thither.* *And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 8:11) Yahusha (Jesus) names the direction, *from the east and west*, and Jeremiah names the same gathering, *from the north country* and *from the coasts of the earth*. The great company that returns is Yashar'el (Israel) coming home to a Father who says *for I am a father to Yashar'el (Israel), and Ephraim is my firstborn* (Jeremiah 31:9).
cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) names the direction, *from the east and west*, and Jeremiah names the same gathering, *from the north country* and *from the coasts of the earth*. The great company that returns is Yashar'el (Israel) coming home to a Father who says *for I am a father to Yashar'el (Israel), and Ephraim is my firstborn* (Jeremiah 31:9).
cards.member_note: Jeremiah 31:8 — *I will bring them from the north country, and gather them from the coasts of the earth.* The great company brought back from the north country and the coasts of the earth is the scattered house of Yashar'el (Israel) coming home.

cards.src_text: And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.
cards.tgt_text: For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Yashar'el (Israel), until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.
cards.old_note: *...many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven* (Matthew 8:11) — said of the centurion's faith, with the children of the kingdom cast out (v.12). The many gathered from east and west are the scattered seed come home from every sphere: the fulness of the Gentiles (Romans 11:25) sat down with the fathers.
cards.note: Romans 11:25 — *For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Yashar'el (Israel), until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.* *And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 8:11) The many who come *from the east and west* to sit with the fathers are the ones Paul has in view when he says blindness in part has come on Yashar'el (Israel) *until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in*. They are the scattered seed, long living as Gentiles among the nations, gathered home from every quarter.
cards.prose: The many who come *from the east and west* to sit with the fathers are the ones Paul has in view when he says blindness in part has come on Yashar'el (Israel) *until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in*. They are the scattered seed, long living as Gentiles among the nations, gathered home from every quarter.
cards.member_note: Romans 11:25 — *that blindness in part is happened to Yashar'el (Israel), until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.* The fulness of the Gentiles coming in is the scattered seed of Yashar'el (Israel) gathered home, the many who sit down with the fathers.

cards.src_text: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying, Himself took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses.
cards.tgt_text: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.
cards.old_note: The Messianic-credential prophecy the healing-ministry authenticates; Yahusha (Jesus) will cite this credential himself at Matt 11:5.
cards.note: Isaiah 35:5 — *Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.* *That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying, Himself took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses.* (Matthew 8:17) The sick and the oppressed are brought, and he heals them all. Isaiah said Elohim (God) *will come and save you* (Isaiah 35:4), and that then *the eyes of the blind shall be opened*. Matthew sets this beside the other word, that he *took our infirmities*, and says both are being fulfilled.
cards.prose: The sick and the oppressed are brought, and he heals them all. Isaiah said Elohim (God) *will come and save you* (Isaiah 35:4), and that then *the eyes of the blind shall be opened*. Matthew sets this beside the other word, that he *took our infirmities*, and says both are being fulfilled.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 35:5 — *Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.* Isaiah's picture of the day Elohim (God) comes to save, with the eyes of the blind opened, is what these healings show.

cards.src_text: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying, Himself took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses.
cards.tgt_text: Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said unto them, Go and shew John again those things which ye do hear and see:
cards.old_note: The future self-citation of the Isaiah 35 credential when Yochanan (John) the Immerser sends from prison.
cards.note: Matthew 11:4 — *Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said unto them, Go and shew John again those things which ye do hear and see:* *That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying, Himself took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses.* (Matthew 8:17) Matthew says the healings fulfil what Isaiah spoke. When John sends from prison to ask whether he is the one, Yahusha (Jesus) does not argue, he sends back *those things which ye do hear and see*. The evening at Peter's house is part of that answer.
cards.prose: Matthew says the healings fulfil what Isaiah spoke. When John sends from prison to ask whether he is the one, Yahusha (Jesus) does not argue, he sends back *those things which ye do hear and see*. The evening at Peter's house is part of that answer.
cards.member_note: Matthew 11:4 — *Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said unto them, Go and shew John again those things which ye do hear and see:* Yahusha (Jesus) answers John in prison by pointing to the same healings Matthew has just shown, as his own credential.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) says unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests; but the Son of Adam has not where to lay his head.
cards.tgt_text: What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of Adam, that thou visitest him?
cards.old_note: *What is mortal man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of Adam, that thou visitest him?* — the son-of-Adam Tanakh-substance the title carries.
cards.note: Psalm 8:4 — *What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of Adam, that thou visitest him?* *And Yahusha (Jesus) says unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests; but the Son of Adam has not where to lay his head.* (Matthew 8:20) The foxes have holes and the birds have nests, but the Son of Adam has nowhere to lie down. David asked what the *son of Adam* is, *that thou visitest him*, and here the visit has come, to a man with no bed in the land he came to.
cards.prose: The foxes have holes and the birds have nests, but the Son of Adam has nowhere to lie down. David asked what the *son of Adam* is, *that thou visitest him*, and here the visit has come, to a man with no bed in the land he came to.
cards.member_note: Psalm 8:4 — *What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of Adam, that thou visitest him?* David asks what the son of Adam is that Elohim (God) should visit him, and in Matthew the visit has come.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) says unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests; but the Son of Adam has not where to lay his head.
cards.tgt_text: Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of Elohim (God).
cards.old_note: *Adam, which was the son of Elohim (God)* — the Lukan genealogy's seed-of-Adam-line-of-promise anchor; the Son of Adam at Matt 8:20 stands in this lineage.
cards.note: Luke 3:38 — *Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of Elohim (God).* *And Yahusha (Jesus) says unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests; but the Son of Adam has not where to lay his head.* (Matthew 8:20) Luke carries the line back until it ends at *the son of Adam, which was the son of Elohim (God)*. When Yahusha (Jesus) calls himself the Son of Adam beside the foxes' holes, he is naming that line, the seed of Adam, and he stands in it with nowhere to lay his head.
cards.prose: Luke carries the line back until it ends at *the son of Adam, which was the son of Elohim (God)*. When Yahusha (Jesus) calls himself the Son of Adam beside the foxes' holes, he is naming that line, the seed of Adam, and he stands in it with nowhere to lay his head.
cards.member_note: Luke 3:38 — *which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of Elohim (God).* Luke's genealogy runs back to Adam, the son of Elohim (God), the lineage the title Son of Adam carries.

cards.src_text: But Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead.
cards.tgt_text: Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee.
cards.old_note: The fifth commandment; the Torah-substance the framework preserves; Yahusha (Jesus) is not abolishing parent-honor at Matt 8:22.
cards.note: Exodus 20:12 — *Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee.* *But Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead.* (Matthew 8:22) The man asks to bury his father, and burying a father is honouring him. Moses wrote *Honour thy father and thy mother* with a promise of long days on the land Yahuah (the LORD) gives, and Yahusha (Jesus) never sets that commandment aside. Whatever his answer means, the fifth commandment stands where it was set.
cards.prose: The man asks to bury his father, and burying a father is honouring him. Moses wrote *Honour thy father and thy mother* with a promise of long days on the land Yahuah (the LORD) gives, and Yahusha (Jesus) never sets that commandment aside. Whatever his answer means, the fifth commandment stands where it was set.
cards.member_note: Exodus 20:12 — *Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee.* The fifth commandment is the Torah ground under the disciple's request, and the answer he is given does not remove it.

cards.src_text: But Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead.
cards.tgt_text: My father made me swear, saying, Lo, I die: in my grave which I have digged for me in the land of Canaan, there shalt thou bury me. Now therefore let me go up, I pray thee, and bury my father, and I will come again.
cards.old_note: *Let me go up, I pray thee, and bury my father* — the patriarchal-burial Tanakh-pattern.
cards.note: Genesis 50:5 — *My father made me swear, saying, Lo, I die: in my grave which I have digged for me in the land of Canaan, there shalt thou bury me. Now therefore let me go up, I pray thee, and bury my father, and I will come again.* *But Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead.* (Matthew 8:22) Joseph said to Pharaoh, *let me go up, I pray thee, and bury my father*, nearly what this disciple asks when he wants first to go and bury his father. Pharaoh granted it and Joseph went up. The request is the fathers' own, and nothing in it is a sin.
cards.prose: Joseph said to Pharaoh, *let me go up, I pray thee, and bury my father*, nearly what this disciple asks when he wants first to go and bury his father. Pharaoh granted it and Joseph went up. The request is the fathers' own, and nothing in it is a sin.
cards.member_note: Genesis 50:5 — *My father made me swear, saying, Lo, I die: in my grave which I have digged for me in the land of Canaan, there shalt thou bury me. Now therefore let me go up, I pray thee, and bury my father, and I will come again.* Joseph asks leave to go up and bury his father and is granted it, the pattern of the fathers behind the disciple's request.

cards.src_text: But Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead.
cards.tgt_text: For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:
cards.old_note: Yahusha's (Jesus's) explicit defense of the fifth commandment against the *Corban* oral-tradition workaround.
cards.note: Mark 7:10 — *For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:* *But Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead.* (Matthew 8:22) In Mark he turns on those who let a man call his goods Corban and so do nothing for father or mother, *Making the word of Elohim (God) of none effect through your tradition* (Mark 7:13). The one who defends the commandment there is the one speaking in Matthew, so his word to this man cannot be a loosing of it.

The one who defends the commandment there is the one speaking in Matthew, so his word to this man cannot be a loosing of it.
cards.member_note: Mark 7:10 — *For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:* Moses said to honour father and mother, and Yahusha (Jesus) defends that commandment against the tradition that emptied it.

cards.src_text: And he says unto them, Why are you fearful, O you of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.
cards.tgt_text: O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of hosts, who is a strong Yahuah (LORD) like unto thee? or to thy faithfulness round about thee?
cards.old_note: *Thou rulest the raging of the sea: when the waves thereof arise, thou stillest them* — the Tanakh-creation-authority of Yahuah (the LORD) the Formed exercises in person.
cards.note: Psalm 89:8 — *O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of hosts, who is a strong Yahuah (LORD) like unto thee? or to thy faithfulness round about thee?* *And he says unto them, Why are you fearful, O you of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.* (Matthew 8:26) The psalm asks who is *like unto thee*, and the next line answers: *Thou rulest the raging of the sea: when the waves thereof arise, thou stillest them* (Psalm 89:9). At the boat the winds and the sea are stilled by a word from the man who was asleep, and the disciples see done what the psalm sang of Yahuah (the LORD).
cards.prose: The psalm asks who is *like unto thee*, and the next line answers: *Thou rulest the raging of the sea: when the waves thereof arise, thou stillest them* (Psalm 89:9). At the boat the winds and the sea are stilled by a word from the man who was asleep, and the disciples see done what the psalm sang of Yahuah (the LORD).
cards.member_note: Psalm 89:8 — *O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of hosts, who is a strong Yahuah (LORD) like unto thee? or to thy faithfulness round about thee?* The psalm asks who is like Yahuah (the LORD) and answers that he rules the raging of the sea, which the disciples see at the boat.

cards.src_text: And he says unto them, Why are you fearful, O you of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.
cards.tgt_text: They that go down to the sea in ships, that do business in great waters;
cards.old_note: The sailors-in-the-storm psalm; *He maketh the storm a calm, so that the waves thereof are still.*
cards.note: Psalm 107:23 — *They that go down to the sea in ships, that do business in great waters;* *And he says unto them, Why are you fearful, O you of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.* (Matthew 8:26) This is the psalm for men in ships, who *see the works of Yahuah (LORD), and his wonders in the deep* (Psalm 107:24). The disciples in the boat are those men, with the waves over the sides, and they see the storm stilled by a word.

cards.member_note: Psalm 107:23 — *They that go down to the sea in ships, that do business in great waters;* Men who go down to the sea in ships see the works of Yahuah (the LORD) in the deep, the same sight the disciples have in the storm.

cards.src_text: And he says unto them, Why are you fearful, O you of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.
cards.tgt_text: Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth, as if it had issued out of the womb?
cards.old_note: *Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further: and here shall thy proud waves be stayed* — the creation-ruling Tanakh-voice the disciples are recognizing.
cards.note: Job 38:8 — *Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth, as if it had issued out of the womb?* *And he says unto them, Why are you fearful, O you of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.* (Matthew 8:26) Job is asked who *shut up the sea with doors*, and the answer comes with the sea's own limit: *Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further* (Job 38:11). The voice that set that boundary is the voice heard from the boat, and the winds and the sea obey it.

cards.src_text: And he says unto them, Why are you fearful, O you of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.
cards.tgt_text: Then the mariners were afraid, and cried every man unto his god, and cast forth the wares that were in the ship into the sea, to lighten it of them. But Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.
cards.old_note: *Yonah (Jonah) was gone down into the sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep* — the Jonah-1 parallel Matt 8:23-27 inverts; the *greater than Yonah (Jonah)* foreshadowing.
cards.note: Jonah 1:5 — *Then the mariners were afraid, and cried every man unto his god, and cast forth the wares that were in the ship into the sea, to lighten it of them. But Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.* *And he says unto them, Why are you fearful, O you of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.* (Matthew 8:26) Both stories have a ship in a great storm and one man asleep. Jonah is *fast asleep* because he is running from Yahuah (the LORD), and the storm was sent after him. Yahusha (Jesus) sleeps in peace, wakes, and stills the sea with a word.
cards.prose: Both stories have a ship in a great storm and one man asleep. Jonah is *fast asleep* because he is running from Yahuah (the LORD), and the storm was sent after him. Yahusha (Jesus) sleeps in peace, wakes, and stills the sea with a word.
cards.member_note: Jonah 1:5 — *But Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.* Jonah sleeps in a ship in a storm sent after him, while Yahusha (Jesus) sleeps in peace and stills the storm himself.

cards.src_text: And he says unto them, Why are you fearful, O you of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.
cards.tgt_text: The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.
cards.old_note: *A greater than Yonah (Jonah) is here* — the future explicit naming of the same foreshadowing.
cards.note: Matthew 12:41 — *The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.* *And he says unto them, Why are you fearful, O you of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.* (Matthew 8:26) In the boat a sleeper wakes and the sea goes calm. Later he says what the boat was showing, *a greater than Jonas is here*, to a generation asking for a sign. The disciples had already seen the sign on the water.

cards.member_note: Matthew 12:41 — *because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.* Yahusha (Jesus) says a greater than Jonas is here, which the stilled sea in the boat had already shown the disciples.

cards.src_text: And, behold, they cried out, saying, What have we to do with you, Yahusha (Jesus), you Son of Elohim (God)? are you come hither to torment us before the time?
cards.tgt_text: Whoever goes on sinning belongs to the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the very beginning. This is why the Son of Elohim (God) was revealed: to undo the works of the devil.
cards.old_note: *For this purpose the Son of Elohim (God) was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil* — the apostolic naming of the King's mission against the principalities; the demons recognize what they are facing.
cards.note: 1 John 3:8 — *Whoever goes on sinning belongs to the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the very beginning. John says that is what the Son was revealed for, and in the country of the Gergesenes the devil's hold on two men is broken in front of the whole city.

cards.src_text: And, behold, they cried out, saying, What have we to do with you, Yahusha (Jesus), you Son of Elohim (God)? are you come hither to torment us before the time?
cards.tgt_text: For if Elohim (God) spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment;
cards.old_note: *Elohim (God) spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment* — the bound-angels-reserved-for-judgment architecture; the *time* the demons reference is this appointed judgment.
cards.note: 2 Peter 2:4 — *For if Elohim (God) spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment;* *And, behold, they cried out, saying, What have we to do with you, Yahusha (Jesus), you Son of Elohim (God)? are you come hither to torment us before the time?* (Matthew 8:29) The cry *before the time* asks about a time already set. Peter says Elohim (God) did not spare the angels that sinned but delivered them into chains *to be reserved unto judgment*, and the spirits in the tombs of the Gergesenes know that same day is waiting for them.
cards.prose: The cry *before the time* asks about a time already set. Peter says Elohim (God) did not spare the angels that sinned but delivered them into chains *to be reserved unto judgment*, and the spirits in the tombs of the Gergesenes know that same day is waiting for them.
cards.member_note: 2 Peter 2:4 — *cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment.* Elohim (God) did not spare the angels that sinned but kept them for judgment, the appointed time the spirits fear in Matthew.

cards.src_text: And, behold, they cried out, saying, What have we to do with you, Yahusha (Jesus), you Son of Elohim (God)? are you come hither to torment us before the time?
cards.tgt_text: And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.
cards.old_note: *And the angels which kept not their first estate ... he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day* — same architecture, same appointed time.
cards.note: Jude 1:6 — *And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.* *And, behold, they cried out, saying, What have we to do with you, Yahusha (Jesus), you Son of Elohim (God)? are you come hither to torment us before the time?* (Matthew 8:29) Jude gives the same reservation a name, *the judgment of the great day*, and the chains kept for the angels who left their own habitation. When the spirits ask if he came *to torment us before the time*, it is that day they have in view.

cards.src_text: And there was a good way off from them an herd of many swine feeding.
cards.tgt_text: And the swine, though he divide the hoof, and be clovenfooted, yet he cheweth not the cud; he is unclean to you.
cards.old_note: The swine as unclean-animals under Torah-law; the visible-marker that the Gergesene/Gadarene territory was under Hellenistic-Gentile administration, not Torah-walking.
cards.note: Leviticus 11:7 — *And the swine, though he divide the hoof, and be clovenfooted, yet he cheweth not the cud; he is unclean to you.* *And there was a good way off from them an herd of many swine feeding.* (Matthew 8:30) The Torah calls the swine *unclean to you*, and a herd of them feeding near the tombs says how far the people of that coast had drifted from it. The spirits ask for the herd, the unclean going into the unclean, and the whole herd runs down into the sea.
cards.prose: The Torah calls the swine *unclean to you*, and a herd of them feeding near the tombs says how far the people of that coast had drifted from it. The spirits ask for the herd, the unclean going into the unclean, and the whole herd runs down into the sea.
cards.member_note: Leviticus 11:7 — *And the swine, though he divide the hoof, and be clovenfooted, yet he cheweth not the cud; he is unclean to you.* Moses names the swine as unclean, so the herd beside the tombs is a plain sign of defilement and of a place living away from the Torah.

cards.src_text: And there was a good way off from them an herd of many swine feeding.
cards.tgt_text: And the swine, because it divideth the hoof, yet cheweth not the cud, it is unclean unto you: ye shall not eat of their flesh, nor touch their dead carcase.
cards.old_note: Second Torah-witness on the swine's unclean status.
cards.note: Deuteronomy 14:8 — *And the swine, because it divideth the hoof, yet cheweth not the cud, it is unclean unto you: ye shall not eat of their flesh, nor touch their dead carcase.* *And there was a good way off from them an herd of many swine feeding.* (Matthew 8:30) Moses says it a second time, and here adds *nor touch their dead carcase*. A herd of the animal the commandment names, feeding by the tombs and then lying dead in the sea, is the very picture the commandment keeps a man away from.
cards.prose: Moses says it a second time, and here adds *nor touch their dead carcase*. A herd of the animal the commandment names, feeding by the tombs and then lying dead in the sea, is the very picture the commandment keeps a man away from.
cards.member_note: Deuteronomy 14:8 — *ye shall not eat of their flesh, nor touch their dead carcase.* A second witness in the Torah that the swine are unclean, adding that even their dead carcase was not to be touched.

cards.src_text: But go you and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
cards.tgt_text: But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.
cards.old_note: Yahusha's (Jesus's) second citation of Hosea 6:6, in the Shabbat-controversy context.
cards.note: Matthew 12:7 — *But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.* *But go you and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.* (Matthew 9:13) Yahusha (Jesus) puts the same words in front of the Pharisees a second time, and again the point is who gets hurt by the rule. At the table they questioned him for sitting with sinners, and here they condemn men over a fence built around the Sabbath, and he says that knowing the words would have stopped it: *ye would not have condemned the guiltless*.
cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) puts the same words in front of the Pharisees a second time, and again the point is who gets hurt by the rule. At the table they questioned him for sitting with sinners, and here they condemn men over a fence built around the Sabbath, and he says that knowing the words would have stopped it: *ye would not have condemned the guiltless*.
cards.member_note: Matthew 12:7 — *But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.* Yahusha (Jesus) hands the same words from Hosea to the Pharisees again, saying that knowing them would have kept them from condemning men who broke no commandment.

cards.src_text: But go you and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
cards.tgt_text: Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required.
cards.old_note: *Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened.*
cards.note: Psalm 40:6 — *Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required.* *But go you and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.* (Matthew 9:13) David says it before the Pharisees did: *Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire*. In the same psalm he says what Yahuah (the LORD) wanted in its place, an opened ear and *thy law is within my heart* (Psalm 40:8). That is the mercy over sacrifice Yahusha (Jesus) sends them to learn, the commandment taken in and kept.
cards.prose: David says it before the Pharisees did: *Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire*. In the same psalm he says what Yahuah (the LORD) wanted in its place, an opened ear and *thy law is within my heart* (Psalm 40:8). That is the mercy over sacrifice Yahusha (Jesus) sends them to learn, the commandment taken in and kept.
cards.member_note: Psalm 40:6 — *Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required.* David says sacrifice and offering were not what Yahuah (the LORD) desired, and that he wanted an opened ear and the law kept within the heart.

cards.src_text: But go you and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
cards.tgt_text: For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering.
cards.old_note: *Thou desirest not sacrifice ... a broken and a contrite heart, O Elohim (God), thou wilt not despise.*
cards.note: Psalm 51:16 — *For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering.* *But go you and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.* (Matthew 9:13) David carries real guilt in this psalm and says a burnt offering would not answer it: *thou delightest not in burnt offering*. What he brings is named in the next verse, *a broken and a contrite heart, O Elohim (God), thou wilt not despise* (Psalm 51:17). That is the sick man the physician comes to, not the whole man who thinks he needs none.

cards.src_text: But go you and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
cards.tgt_text: To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith Yahuah (LORD): I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats.
cards.old_note: *To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? ... cease to do evil; learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed.*
cards.note: Isaiah 1:11 — *To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith Yahuah (LORD): I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats.* *But go you and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.* (Matthew 9:13) The question is Yahuah's (the LORD's) own: *To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me?* The altar was full, and the verse before it sends the people back to *the law of our Elohim (God)* (Isaiah 1:10), which is where Yahusha (Jesus) sends the Pharisees when he tells them to go and learn.

cards.member_note: Isaiah 1:11 — *I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats.* Yahuah (the LORD) asks what purpose a multitude of sacrifices serves when he is already full of them and takes no delight in the blood.

cards.src_text: But go you and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
cards.tgt_text: Thus saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel); Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh.
cards.old_note: *I spake not unto your fathers ... concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices: But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice.*
cards.note: Jeremiah 7:21 — *Thus saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel); Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh.* *But go you and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.* (Matthew 9:13) Here Yahuah (the LORD) answers an offering that had come loose from obeying him: *Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh*. What he asked at the beginning was *Obey my voice, and I will be your Elohim (God), and ye shall be my people* (Jeremiah 7:23), the thing the Pharisees at the table had put second.

cards.src_text: But go you and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
cards.tgt_text: I hate, I despise your feast days, and I will not smell in your solemn assemblies.
cards.old_note: *I hate, I despise your feast days ... But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.*

cards.src_text: But go you and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
cards.tgt_text: Wherewith shall I come before Yahuah (LORD), and bow myself before the high Elohim (God)? shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves of a year old?
cards.old_note: *He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good ... to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy Elohim (God).*
cards.note: Micah 6:6 — *Wherewith shall I come before Yahuah (LORD), and bow myself before the high Elohim (God)? shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves of a year old?* *But go you and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.* (Matthew 9:13) A worshipper asks whether he comes before Yahuah (the LORD) with burnt offerings and calves of a year old, and the answer comes two verses on: *what doth Yahuah (LORD) require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy Elohim (God)?* (Micah 6:8). cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Can the children of the bridechamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then shall they fast.
cards.tgt_text: And I will betroth thee unto me for ever; yea, I will betroth thee unto me in righteousness, and in judgment, and in lovingkindness, and in mercies.
cards.old_note: The betrothal-restoration of divorced-Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.note: Hosea 2:19 — *And I will betroth thee unto me for ever; yea, I will betroth thee unto me in righteousness, and in judgment, and in lovingkindness, and in mercies.* *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Can the children of the bridechamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then shall they fast.* (Matthew 9:15) The bridegroom Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of is no stranger to the room. Yahuah (the LORD) had already said to the scattered house of Yashar'el (Israel), *I will betroth thee unto me for ever*, and the gifts he names are *in righteousness, and in judgment, and in lovingkindness, and in mercies*. The mercy he asks at the table is the mercy of the wedding.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Can the children of the bridechamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then shall they fast.
cards.tgt_text: For thy Maker is thine husband; Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel); The Elohim (God) of the whole earth shall he be called.
cards.old_note: *Thy Maker is thine husband; Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) is his name.*
cards.note: Isaiah 54:5 — *For thy Maker is thine husband; Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel); The Elohim (God) of the whole earth shall he be called.* *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Can the children of the bridechamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then shall they fast.* (Matthew 9:15) The husband here is Yahuah (the LORD) himself: *For thy Maker is thine husband*. He speaks to *a woman forsaken and grieved in spirit* (Isaiah 54:6) and says *with great mercies will I gather thee* (Isaiah 54:7). So the bridegroom among the children of the bridechamber is the husband who gathers.

cards.src_text: And when Yahusha (Jesus) departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, You Son of David, have mercy on us.
cards.tgt_text: And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots:
cards.old_note: *A Branch shall grow out of his roots* — the Davidic-shoot prophecy.
cards.note: Isaiah 11:1 — *And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots:* *And when Yahusha (Jesus) departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, You Son of David, have mercy on us.* (Matthew 9:27) The two blind men call him *Thou Son of David*, and Isaiah gave that name its root: *a Branch shall grow out of his roots*. The verse after says *In his days Yahudah (Judah) shall be saved, and Yashar'el (Israel) shall dwell safely* (Jeremiah 23:6), so the one they cry to is king over both houses.

cards.src_text: And when Yahusha (Jesus) departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, You Son of David, have mercy on us.
cards.tgt_text: And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd.
cards.old_note: *My servant David* as the Messianic-shepherd.
cards.note: Ezekiel 34:23 — *And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd.* *And when Yahusha (Jesus) departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, You Son of David, have mercy on us.* (Matthew 9:27) Ezekiel names what was done to the sick of the flock, *pushed all the diseased with your horns, till ye have scattered them abroad* (Ezekiel 34:21), and then promises *one shepherd over them*, even David. Two blind men crying for mercy to the Son of David are two of those diseased ones, and he is the shepherd who was promised.

cards.src_text: And when Yahusha (Jesus) departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, You Son of David, have mercy on us.

The king the blind men cry to leads people back into the commandments, not out of them.

She calls him by the title of Yashar'el's (Israel's) king because she is one of the sheep he says he is sent to, *the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Matthew 15:24).

cards.src_text: And when Yahusha (Jesus) departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, You Son of David, have mercy on us.
cards.tgt_text: And the multitudes that went before, and that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of Yahuah (Lord); Hosanna in the highest.
cards.old_note: The triumphal-entry crowds' *Hosanna to the Son of David* — the moment the marginalized-recognition becomes the collective-acclamation.
cards.note: Matthew 21:9 — *And the multitudes that went before, and that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of Yahuah (Lord); Hosanna in the highest.* *And when Yahusha (Jesus) departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, You Son of David, have mercy on us.* (Matthew 9:27) What two blind men cried at his heels a whole crowd now cries before him and behind him, *Hosanna to the Son of David*, and they add that he comes *in the name of Yahuah (Lord)*. The title is no longer asked for mercy by a few; it is said over him by the multitudes.

cards.src_text: But that you may know that the Son of Adam has power on earth to forgive sins, (then says he to the sick of the palsy,) Arise, take up your bed, and go unto your house.
cards.tgt_text: I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.
cards.old_note: The kaph-comparative *one like the Son of Adam* (incarnation-honoring; harmonized identification is Yahusha (Jesus) himself, the Formed cloud-rider who took on flesh) — the figure to whom all dominion is given; the same figure exercising the forgiveness-prerogative on earth at Matt 9:6.
cards.note: Daniel 7:13 — *I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.* *But that you may know that the Son of Adam has power on earth to forgive sins, (then says he to the sick of the palsy,) Arise, take up your bed, and go unto your house.* (Matthew 9:6) The title Yahusha (Jesus) takes at the sick man's bed is Daniel's. Daniel saw *one like the Son of Adam* before the Ancient of days, and the next verse says what was given him, *dominion, and glory, and a kingdom* (Daniel 7:14). He took on flesh, and that authority is what he uses over the man's sins.

cards.src_text: But that you may know that the Son of Adam has power on earth to forgive sins, (then says he to the sick of the palsy,) Arise, take up your bed, and go unto your house.
cards.tgt_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.
cards.old_note: *All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth* — the full-disclosure of the authority the Son of Adam already exercised at Matt 9:6.
cards.note: Matthew 28:18 — *And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* *But that you may know that the Son of Adam has power on earth to forgive sins, (then says he to the sick of the palsy,) Arise, take up your bed, and go unto your house.* (Matthew 9:6) At the bed he claimed *power on earth* to forgive sins, and the multitudes *glorified Elohim (God), which had given such power unto men* (Matthew 9:8). On the mountain in Galilee he says the rest of it, *All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth*, so the authority shown over one man's sins reaches over everything.

cards.src_text: But go you and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
cards.tgt_text: For the Son of Adam is come to seek and to save that which was lost.

cards.src_text: Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break, and the wine runs out, and the bottles perish: but they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved.
cards.tgt_text: A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.
cards.old_note: The new-heart and new-spirit Tanakh-promise — the new-wineskin container the heart-Torah-walking life requires.
cards.note: Ezekiel 36:26 — *A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.* *Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break, and the wine runs out, and the bottles perish: but they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved.* (Matthew 9:17) New wine needs a new container, and Ezekiel says what it is, *a new heart* and *a new spirit*. The wine is not a different law, since the next verse says the spirit will *cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them* (Ezekiel 36:27). The bottle that cannot hold that is the one that breaks.

cards.src_text: Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break, and the wine runs out, and the bottles perish: but they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved.
cards.tgt_text: Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.
cards.old_note: The load-bearing anti-antinomian declaration of the Sermon — locks the Torah-affirmation that Matt 9:17 cannot be reread to undo.
cards.note: Matthew 5:17 — *Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.* *Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break, and the wine runs out, and the bottles perish: but they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved.* (Matthew 9:17) The new wine is not a new law. Yahusha (Jesus) had already said *I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil*, and that *one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law* (Matthew 5:18). What cannot hold the wine is a system built on fences, so the container changes and the wine does not.

cards.member_note: Matthew 5:17 — *Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.* Yahusha (Jesus) says he has not come to destroy the law or the prophets, so the new wine is not a new law.

cards.src_text: But Yahusha (Jesus) turned him about, and when he saw her, he said, Daughter, be of good comfort; your faith has made you whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour.
cards.tgt_text: And if a woman have an issue of her blood many days out of the time of her separation, or if it run beyond the time of her separation; all the days of the issue of her uncleanness shall be as the days of her separation: she shall be unclean.
cards.old_note: The Torah's purity-rules on chronic-discharge that had categorically-isolated the woman for twelve years.
cards.note: Leviticus 15:25 — *And if a woman have an issue of her blood many days out of the time of her separation, or if it run beyond the time of her separation; all the days of the issue of her uncleanness shall be as the days of her separation: she shall be unclean.* *But Yahusha (Jesus) turned him about, and when he saw her, he said, Daughter, be of good comfort; your faith has made you whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour.* (Matthew 9:22) Twelve years of this: the Torah's rule for an issue of blood that runs past its time, *she shall be unclean*. She comes behind him and touches the hem anyway, and her uncleanness does not pass to him; the wholeness passes to her. He did not break the commandment, and he is the one who gave it.

cards.member_note: Leviticus 15:25 — *all the days of the issue of her uncleanness shall be as the days of her separation: she shall be unclean.* The Torah's rule on an issue of blood that runs long, which kept the woman unclean for the twelve years she bled.

cards.src_text: But Yahusha (Jesus) turned him about, and when he saw her, he said, Daughter, be of good comfort; your faith has made you whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour.
cards.tgt_text: And, behold, there came a leper and worshipped him, saying, Adonai (Lord), if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
cards.old_note: The leper-pericope at the same anti-defilement pattern — the King as cleansing-source.
cards.note: Matthew 8:2 — *And, behold, there came a leper and worshipped him, saying, Adonai (Lord), if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.* *But Yahusha (Jesus) turned him about, and when he saw her, he said, Daughter, be of good comfort; your faith has made you whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour.* (Matthew 9:22) A leper and a bleeding woman both stand outside by the Torah's own rules, and both come to him. He touches the leper, and the cleanness goes out from him instead of the uncleanness coming in. Then he sends the man to *shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded* (Matthew 8:4), the commandment kept.

cards.src_text: He said unto them, Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleeps. And they laughed him to scorn.
cards.tgt_text: And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
cards.old_note: *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake* — the Tanakh's resurrection-language.
cards.note: Daniel 12:2 — *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* *He said unto them, Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleeps. And they laughed him to scorn.* (Matthew 9:24) The mourners laugh when he says the maid is not dead, *but sleepeth*, yet it is Daniel's own way of speaking of the dead, those who *sleep in the dust of the earth*. For a girl in one house the waking is that he *took her by the hand, and the maid arose* (Matthew 9:25).
cards.prose: The mourners laugh when he says the maid is not dead, *but sleepeth*, yet it is Daniel's own way of speaking of the dead, those who *sleep in the dust of the earth*. For a girl in one house the waking is that he *took her by the hand, and the maid arose* (Matthew 9:25).
cards.member_note: Daniel 12:2 — *many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake.* Daniel says many who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, the word Yahusha (Jesus) uses of the ruler's daughter.

cards.src_text: He said unto them, Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleeps. And they laughed him to scorn.
cards.tgt_text: Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise. Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust: for thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead.
cards.old_note: *Thy dead men shall live ... Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust.* The resurrection-prophecy Yahusha (Jesus) carries the present-age-foretaste of at 9:25.
cards.note: Isaiah 26:19 — *Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise. Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust: for thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead.* *He said unto them, Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleeps. And they laughed him to scorn.* (Matthew 9:24) Isaiah speaks to the dead as sleepers who can be called up, *Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust*, and says *the earth shall cast out the dead*. At the ruler's house he says the maid sleeps and she rises when he takes her by the hand. What the prophet sets at the end of the age shows here in one house, for one girl.

cards.src_text: He said unto them, Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleeps. And they laughed him to scorn.
cards.tgt_text: These things said he: and after that he saith unto them, Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep.
cards.old_note: *Lazaros (Lazarus) sleepeth; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep.* The same death-as-sleep vocabulary at the Lazaros-raising.
cards.note: John 11:11 — *These things said he: and after that he saith unto them, Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep.* *He said unto them, Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleeps. And they laughed him to scorn.* (Matthew 9:24) He says *sleepeth* of someone who is dead, just as he did of the ruler's daughter, and again the people around him do not take it as he means it, the mourners laughing and the disciples thinking Lazarus is only resting. For him death is a sleep he can wake a man from: *that I may awake him out of sleep*.

cards.src_text: He said unto them, Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleeps. And they laughed him to scorn.
cards.tgt_text: But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope.
cards.old_note: The early-assembly's continuation of the sleep-and-awakening eschatological-framing.
cards.note: 1 Thessalonians 4:13 — *But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope.* *He said unto them, Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleeps. And they laughed him to scorn.* (Matthew 9:24) Paul uses the same word for the dead that Yahusha (Jesus) used at the girl's bedside, *asleep*, and writes that the grieving should *sorrow not, even as others which have no hope*. The mourners laughed at the one who said it; Paul hands on what he knew, that the sleep has a waking.
cards.prose: Paul uses the same word for the dead that Yahusha (Jesus) used at the girl's bedside, *asleep*, and writes that the grieving should *sorrow not, even as others which have no hope*. The mourners laughed at the one who said it; Paul hands on what he knew, that the sleep has a waking.
cards.member_note: 1 Thessalonians 4:13 — *concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope.* Paul will not have the brethren ignorant about those who are asleep, so that they do not sorrow as people without hope.

cards.src_text: But the Pharisees said, He casts out devils through the prince of the devils.
cards.tgt_text: Then was brought unto him one possessed with a devil, blind, and dumb: and he healed him, insomuch that the blind and dumb both spake and saw.
cards.old_note: The dismantling of the same slander; the self-contradicting nature of the Beelzebul-attribution made explicit.
cards.note: Matthew 12:22 — *Then was brought unto him one possessed with a devil, blind, and dumb: and he healed him, insomuch that the blind and dumb both spake and saw.* *But the Pharisees said, He casts out devils through the prince of the devils.* (Matthew 9:34) A man both blind and dumb is brought to him and healed so that *the blind and dumb both spake and saw*, and the charge about the prince of the devils follows at once, as it did in Matthew 9. This time he answers it: *Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation* (Matthew 12:25).
cards.prose: A man both blind and dumb is brought to him and healed so that *the blind and dumb both spake and saw*, and the charge about the prince of the devils follows at once, as it did in Matthew 9. cards.member_note: Matthew 12:22 — *he healed him, insomuch that the blind and dumb both spake and saw.* A man both blind and dumb is healed so that he speaks and sees, and the same charge about the prince of the devils follows.

cards.src_text: But the Pharisees said, He casts out devils through the prince of the devils.
cards.tgt_text: Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) shall not be forgiven unto men.
cards.old_note: The blasphemy-against-the-Ruach warning that the Matt 9:34 attribution-failure trajectory leads toward.
cards.note: Matthew 12:31 — *Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) shall not be forgiven unto men.* *But the Pharisees said, He casts out devils through the prince of the devils.* (Matthew 9:34) When the charge about the prince of the devils is allowed to stand, this is where it leads. *Whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of Adam, it shall be forgiven him* (Matthew 12:32), but naming the work of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) as the devils' work is *the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit)*, which shall not be forgiven.

cards.src_text: But the Pharisees said, He casts out devils through the prince of the devils.
cards.tgt_text: And Ahaziah fell down through a lattice in his upper chamber that was in Samaria, and was sick: and he sent messengers, and said unto them, Go, enquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron whether I shall recover of this disease.
cards.old_note: The *Ba'al Zevuv* (Beelzebul / lord of the flies) Philistine-name preserved in the Tanakh as a Pharisaic-rhetoric source.
cards.note: 2 Kings 1:2 — *And Ahaziah fell down through a lattice in his upper chamber that was in Samaria, and was sick: and he sent messengers, and said unto them, Go, enquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron whether I shall recover of this disease.* *But the Pharisees said, He casts out devils through the prince of the devils.* (Matthew 9:34) When Matthew gives the charge in full it has a name, *but by Beelzebub the prince of the devils* (Matthew 12:24), and the name is older than the Pharisees. A king of Samaria sent to ask *Baal-zebub the god of Ekron* whether he would recover, when he should have asked Yahuah (the LORD). The charge borrows that name and puts it on the one who casts devils out.

The charge borrows that name and puts it on the one who casts devils out.
cards.member_note: 2 Kings 1:2 — *enquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron whether I shall recover of this disease.* A king of Samaria sends to Baal-zebub the god of Ekron to ask whether he will recover, the name behind the charge of the prince of the devils.

cards.src_text: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.
cards.tgt_text: For the idols have spoken vanity, and the diviners have seen a lie, and have told false dreams; they comfort in vain: therefore they went their way as a flock, they were troubled, because there was no shepherd.
cards.old_note: *They went their way as a flock, they were troubled, because there was no shepherd.*
cards.note: Zechariah 10:2 — *For the idols have spoken vanity, and the diviners have seen a lie, and have told false dreams; they comfort in vain: therefore they went their way as a flock, they were troubled, because there was no shepherd.* *But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.* (Matthew 9:36) Matthew's *scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd* is Zechariah's picture of a people who *went their way as a flock*. Idols and diviners comforted *in vain*, and the next verse turns on the shepherds, *Mine anger was kindled against the shepherds* (Zechariah 10:3).

cards.src_text: Then says he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;
cards.tgt_text: Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest.
cards.old_note: *The fields ... are white already to harvest.* The same harvest-language at the Samaritan-woman pericope.
cards.note: John 4:35 — *Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest.* *Then says he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;* (Matthew 9:37) The harvest he calls plenteous in Matthew, he tells his disciples to see for themselves, to *Lift up your eyes* because the fields are *white already to harvest*. The ripeness is there before they have done anything, and he says they enter in where *other men laboured, and ye are entered into their labours* (John 4:38).

cards.member_note: John 4:35 — *Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest.* He tells his disciples the fields are already white to harvest, the same harvest he calls plenteous.

cards.src_text: Then says he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;
cards.tgt_text: And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.
cards.old_note: The immediate-next-verse commission of the twelve — the answer to the prayer Yahusha (Jesus) just instructed.
cards.note: Matthew 10:1 — *And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.* *Then says he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;* (Matthew 9:37) The twelve are the answer to the prayer. He had just said *the labourers are few*, and now he calls twelve and gives them power *against unclean spirits*, and over every sickness, the work he had been doing himself in every city and village. They are given his own work to do.
cards.prose: The twelve are the answer to the prayer. He had just said *the labourers are few*, and now he calls twelve and gives them power *against unclean spirits*, and over every sickness, the work he had been doing himself in every city and village. They are given his own work to do.

cards.src_text: And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.
cards.tgt_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.old_note: *Ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel)* — the eschatological-promise that locks the twelve-apostle / twelve-tribe correspondence.
cards.note: Matthew 19:28 — *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* *And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.* (Matthew 10:1) Count the men he has just called and count the tribes, and it comes out twelve and twelve. Here he says what the match is for. The men who have followed him will sit on *twelve thrones*, and what they judge is all the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel), not one house of it. The sending in Matthew is the first of that work.
cards.prose: Count the men he has just called and count the tribes, and it comes out twelve and twelve. Here he says what the match is for. cards.src_text: And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.

The men who share his table in the kingdom are the men who sit on thrones over the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel). He sent them out with power in Matthew, and this is where the road was always headed for them.

cards.src_text: And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.

The men he sent out with power were no passing crew, since they are part of what the city stands on.

What the twelve go out to gather is what the gates are named for.
