cards.src_text: And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.
cards.tgt_text: Afterward he brought me again unto the door of the house; and, behold, waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward: for the forefront of the house stood toward the east, and the waters came down from under from the right side of the house, at the south side of the altar.
cards.old_note: The millennial-twelve-tribe land-allotment Yechezk'el details in the restoration-vision.
cards.note: Ezekiel 47:1 — *Afterward he brought me again unto the door of the house; and, behold, waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward: for the forefront of the house stood toward the east, and the waters came down from under from the right side of the house, at the south side of the altar.* *And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.* (Matthew 10:1) The tribes the twelve are sent to gather are headed somewhere. Ezekiel is shown the house restored, and *waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward*. The vision of the tribes in their land has this house at its center, with the water running out from it.
cards.prose: The tribes the twelve are sent to gather are headed somewhere. Ezekiel is shown the house restored, and *waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward*. The vision of the tribes in their land has this house at its center, with the water running out from it.
cards.member_note: Ezekiel 47:1 — *waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward.* Ezekiel sees water running out from under the threshold of the restored house, the place the gathered tribes are brought to.

cards.src_text: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when you depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.
cards.tgt_text: Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.
cards.old_note: *Cast not your pearls before swine* — the parallel discrimination-principle at the broader-pearl-level; the same disposition of not-wasting-substance-on-unworthy-receivers.
cards.note: Matthew 7:6 — *Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.* *And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when you depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.* (Matthew 10:14) He said this to the crowd on the mountain, and here he gives the twelve the same teaching in walking shoes. What is holy is not pressed on those who trample it. When a house will not hear, the twelve shake off the dust and go on, and they do not chase a hearing that has been refused.
cards.prose: He said this to the crowd on the mountain, and here he gives the twelve the same teaching in walking shoes. What is holy is not pressed on those who trample it. When a house will not hear, the twelve shake off the dust and go on, and they do not chase a hearing that has been refused.
cards.member_note: Matthew 7:6 — *neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet.* On the mountain he teaches that what is holy is not pressed on those who trample it.

cards.src_text: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when you depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.
cards.tgt_text: And, behold, the whole city came out to meet Yahusha (Jesus): and when they saw him, they besought him that he would depart out of their coasts.
cards.old_note: The Gergesene townspeople asking the King to leave; the implicit-modeling of the response Matt 10:14 will codify.
cards.note: Matthew 8:34 — *And, behold, the whole city came out to meet Yahusha (Jesus): and when they saw him, they besought him that he would depart out of their coasts.* *And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when you depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.* (Matthew 10:14) The whole city came out, saw him, and asked him to leave, and he went. He did not force himself on them. That is the pattern he gives the twelve for any town that *shall not receive you*. They say what they were sent to say, and if it is refused they go.
cards.prose: The whole city came out, saw him, and asked him to leave, and he went. He did not force himself on them. That is the pattern he gives the twelve for any town that *shall not receive you*. They say what they were sent to say, and if it is refused they go.
cards.member_note: Matthew 8:34 — *they besought him that he would depart out of their coasts.* A whole city asks him to leave its coasts, and he leaves, which is the pattern for the twelve.

cards.src_text: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when you depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.
cards.tgt_text: But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came unto Iconium.
cards.old_note: Direct apostolic-application by Paul and Bar-Naba (Barnabas).
cards.note: Acts 13:51 — *But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came unto Iconium.* *And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when you depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.* (Matthew 10:14) Years later Paul and Barnabas do just what he told the twelve. They shake off the dust and *came unto Iconium*. It is no retreat, since the verse ends with them arriving in the next city. The sheep are scattered, and when one door shuts they go on looking for the ones who will hear.

cards.member_note: Acts 13:51 — *But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came unto Iconium.* Paul and Barnabas shake off the dust against a city and go on to Iconium.

cards.src_text: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when you depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.
cards.tgt_text: And when they opposed themselves, and blasphemed, he shook his raiment, and said unto them, Your blood be upon your own heads; I am clean: from henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles.
cards.old_note: Paul at Corinth: *I am clean: from henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles* — the same shake-the-dust-off pattern at the synagogue-rejection.
cards.note: Acts 18:6 — *And when they opposed themselves, and blasphemed, he shook his raiment, and said unto them, Your blood be upon your own heads; I am clean: from henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles.* *And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when you depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.* (Matthew 10:14) At Corinth the synagogue turned on Paul and spoke against him, so he shook out his clothes and said *I am clean*. He had said what he came to say. The turning to the Gentiles is a change of door, since Paul's field was the scattered house of Yashar'el (Israel) living out among the nations, and the same Shepherd is looking for them there.

cards.src_text: Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.

Then he says Sodom will have it lighter in the day of judgment than the town that would not hear the men he sent. A refused word weighs more than a city that was burned.

cards.src_text: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;
cards.tgt_text: And he goeth up into a mountain, and calleth unto him whom he would: and they came unto him.
cards.old_note: The parallel naming in Mark.
cards.note: Mark 3:13 — *And he goeth up into a mountain, and calleth unto him whom he would: and they came unto him.* *Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;* (Matthew 10:2) Matthew lists them and Mark says how they became twelve. He went up into a mountain and called *whom he would*, and *they came unto him*. The twelve were picked by him and not by their own asking, and the power in Matthew's verse was given to men he had chosen first.
cards.prose: Matthew lists them and Mark says how they became twelve. He went up into a mountain and called *whom he would*, and *they came unto him*. The twelve were picked by him and not by their own asking, and the power in Matthew's verse was given to men he had chosen first.
cards.member_note: Mark 3:13 — *And he goeth up into a mountain, and calleth unto him whom he would: and they came unto him.* Mark shows him going up a mountain and calling the twelve to himself, whom he would, and they came.

cards.src_text: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;
cards.tgt_text: And it came to pass in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to Elohim (God).
cards.old_note: The parallel naming in Luke, after the all-night prayer.
cards.note: Luke 6:12 — *And it came to pass in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to Elohim (God).* *Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;* (Matthew 10:2) Before the names there was a night. Luke has him on the mountain *all night in prayer to Elohim (God)* before he called anyone. The twelve Matthew lists were chosen only after he had spent the night in prayer.

cards.member_note: Luke 6:12 — *went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to Elohim (God).* Luke has him pray all night on the mountain before he chooses the twelve.

cards.src_text: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;
cards.tgt_text: And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.
cards.old_note: The post-resurrection eleven-named (before Mattityahu's [Matthias's] addition at Acts 1:26).
cards.note: Acts 1:13 — *And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.* *Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;* (Matthew 10:2) Set the two lists side by side and the same men are in both, with one gone. Matthew ends his list on Judas Iscariot, who betrayed him, and the room in Acts holds eleven names. The twelve were sent out with power, and the gap shows that one of them did not stay with it.
cards.prose: Set the two lists side by side and the same men are in both, with one gone. Matthew ends his list on Judas Iscariot, who betrayed him, and the room in Acts holds eleven names. The twelve were sent out with power, and the gap shows that one of them did not stay with it.
cards.member_note: Acts 1:13 — *and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.* After the resurrection eleven of the men are named in the upper room, with the place of the one who betrayed him empty.

cards.src_text: These twelve Yahusha (Jesus) sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter you not:
cards.tgt_text: But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Matthew 15:24 — *But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* *These twelve Yahusha (Jesus) sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter you not:* (Matthew 10:5) The reach he gives the twelve is the reach he states to the woman crying after him: *the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)*. She is not sent away in the end, since her daughter is healed, and her coast is the very ground where the scattered house was swallowed up. She is one of the sheep he said he was sent to.
cards.prose: The reach he gives the twelve is the reach he states to the woman crying after him: *the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)*. cards.src_text: These twelve Yahusha (Jesus) sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter you not:
cards.tgt_text: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Messiah (Christ): for it is the power of Elohim (God) unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Yahudi (Jew) first, and also to the Greek.
cards.old_note: Paul's *to the Yahudi (Jew) first, and also to the Greek* — read in framework continuity as the scattered-seed-in-the-nations-territories gathering.
cards.note: Romans 1:16 — *For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Messiah (Christ): for it is the power of Elohim (God) unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Yahudi (Jew) first, and also to the Greek.* *These twelve Yahusha (Jesus) sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter you not:* (Matthew 10:5) Paul's order is the order Yahusha (Jesus) gave the twelve: *to the Yahudi (Jew) first, and also to the Greek*. First the house in the land, then the same scattered house out among the Greeks. He is not naming two kinds of people there, only two places where the lost sheep are found.
cards.prose: Paul's order is the order Yahusha (Jesus) gave the twelve: *to the Yahudi (Jew) first, and also to the Greek*. First the house in the land, then the same scattered house out among the Greeks. He is not naming two kinds of people there, only two places where the lost sheep are found.
cards.member_note: Romans 1:16 — *to every one that believeth; to the Yahudi (Jew) first, and also to the Greek.* Paul keeps the order of the sending, the Yahudi (Jew) first and then the Greek, the house in the land and then the scattered house abroad.

cards.src_text: These twelve Yahusha (Jesus) sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter you not:
cards.tgt_text: Now I say that Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of Elohim (God), to confirm the promises made unto the fathers:
cards.old_note: *Now I say that Yahusha (Jesus) Christ was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of Elohim (God), to confirm the promises made unto the fathers* — Paul's framework-statement of the King's mission-scope.
cards.note: Romans 15:8 — *Now I say that Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of Elohim (God), to confirm the promises made unto the fathers:* *These twelve Yahusha (Jesus) sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter you not:* (Matthew 10:5) Paul says in his own words what the sending says. Yahusha (Jesus) came to the circumcision, the sons of the fathers, so that what was promised to the fathers would be made good. The twelve go to the house of Yashar'el (Israel) because that is where the promise was aimed.

cards.member_note: Romans 15:8 — *was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of Elohim (God), to confirm the promises made unto the fathers.* Paul says Yahusha (Jesus) was a minister of the circumcision to confirm the promises made to the fathers.

cards.src_text: Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely you have received, freely give.
cards.tgt_text: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.
cards.old_note: The Messianic-credential prophecy now extended to the apostolic-mission.
cards.note: Isaiah 35:5 — *Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.* *Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely you have received, freely give.* (Matthew 10:8) The things he tells the twelve to do were already written in Isaiah as the signs of the day Elohim (God) comes and saves. *The eyes of the blind shall be opened*, the prophet says. When the twelve heal, they carry what Isaiah said would mark that day.
cards.prose: The things he tells the twelve to do were already written in Isaiah as the signs of the day Elohim (God) comes and saves. *The eyes of the blind shall be opened*, the prophet says. When the twelve heal, they carry what Isaiah said would mark that day.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 35:5 — *Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.* Isaiah foretells the eyes of the blind opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped when Elohim (God) comes to save.

cards.src_text: Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely you have received, freely give.
cards.tgt_text: The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.
cards.old_note: Yahusha (Jesus) citing the same Isaiah 35 credential to Yochanan's (John's) prison-question — the credential is consistent across the King's-ministry and the apostles'-mission.
cards.note: Matthew 11:5 — *The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.* *Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely you have received, freely give.* (Matthew 10:8) John sent his disciples to ask whether he was the one who should come. Yahusha (Jesus) answered with a list, and it is the list he has just handed the twelve: *the lepers are cleansed*, *the dead are raised up*. What he gave John for an answer is the work he gives them to do.
cards.prose: John sent his disciples to ask whether he was the one who should come. Yahusha (Jesus) answered with a list, and it is the list he has just handed the twelve: *the lepers are cleansed*, *the dead are raised up*. What he gave John for an answer is the work he gives them to do.
cards.member_note: Matthew 11:5 — *the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.* Yahusha (Jesus) answers John's question with the same works he has just given the twelve power to do.

cards.src_text: Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely you have received, freely give.
cards.tgt_text: And when Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles’ hands the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) was given, he offered them money,
cards.old_note: Kefa's (Peter's) rebuke of Shim'on (Simon) the sorcerer for trying to buy the Ruach (Spirit)'s gift — the freely-give principle defended against the monetization-attempt.
cards.note: Acts 8:18 — *And when Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles’ hands the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) was given, he offered them money,* *Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely you have received, freely give.* (Matthew 10:8) *Freely ye have received, freely give.* Simon saw the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) given by the laying on of hands and *offered them money*. He wanted to buy what the twelve were told to hand out for nothing. Peter will not take it, and the gift stays what it was, not for sale.
cards.prose: *Freely ye have received, freely give.* Simon saw the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) given by the laying on of hands and *offered them money*. He wanted to buy what the twelve were told to hand out for nothing. Peter will not take it, and the gift stays what it was, not for sale.
cards.member_note: Acts 8:18 — *And when Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles’ hands the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) was given, he offered them money,* Simon offers money for the gift of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), the one thing the twelve were told to give freely.

cards.src_text: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when you depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.
cards.tgt_text: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear you, when ye depart thence, shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them. Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.
cards.old_note: The parallel shake-the-dust-off instruction.
cards.note: Mark 6:11 — *And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear you, when ye depart thence, shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them. Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.* *And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when you depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.* (Matthew 10:14) Mark gives the same instruction almost word for word, and he adds what the dust is for: *a testimony against them*. Shaking it off is a witness that the word was brought to that town and refused. Like Matthew, Mark ends the verse on Sodom.
cards.prose: Mark gives the same instruction almost word for word, and he adds what the dust is for: *a testimony against them*. Shaking it off is a witness that the word was brought to that town and refused. Like Matthew, Mark ends the verse on Sodom.
cards.member_note: Mark 6:11 — *shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them.* Mark gives the same instruction and names what the dust is for, a testimony against that town, with Sodom set beside it.

cards.src_text: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when you depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.
cards.tgt_text: And whosoever will not receive you, when ye go out of that city, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.
cards.old_note: The parallel in Luke.
cards.note: Luke 9:5 — *And whosoever will not receive you, when ye go out of that city, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.* *And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when you depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.* (Matthew 10:14) Luke has the same instruction, and he marks the place for it. The dust comes off *when ye go out of that city*, on the way out. It is done quietly, and what is left behind is a testimony.
cards.prose: Luke has the same instruction, and he marks the place for it. The dust comes off *when ye go out of that city*, on the way out. It is done quietly, and what is left behind is a testimony.
cards.member_note: Luke 9:5 — *shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.* Luke has the same instruction, with the dust shaken off as they leave the city, for a testimony against it.

cards.src_text: Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.
cards.tgt_text: And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.
cards.old_note: Yahusha's (Jesus's) parallel statement against Kfar-Nachum (Capernaum) at the same eschatological-graduated-accountability frame.
cards.note: Matthew 11:23 — *And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.* *Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.* (Matthew 10:15) He says it again over Capernaum, a town that had seen his works. If those *mighty works* had been done in Sodom, he says, it would still be standing. The more a town has been shown, the more it answers for, and that is what the twelve are told about the town that will not receive them.
cards.prose: He says it again over Capernaum, a town that had seen his works. If those *mighty works* had been done in Sodom, he says, it would still be standing. The more a town has been shown, the more it answers for, and that is what the twelve are told about the town that will not receive them.
cards.member_note: Matthew 11:23 — *if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.* Capernaum is told it will answer for more than Sodom, because Sodom never saw the works done there.

cards.src_text: Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be you therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.
cards.tgt_text: And the dove came in to him in the evening; and, lo, in her mouth was an olive leaf pluckt off: so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.
cards.old_note: The dove of the new-creation-after-the-flood.
cards.note: Genesis 8:11 — *And the dove came in to him in the evening; and, lo, in her mouth was an olive leaf pluckt off: so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.* *Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be you therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.* (Matthew 10:16) The dove in Noah's story came back in the evening with an olive leaf, and that told Noah the waters were going down. A dove carries news and does no harm. When Yahusha (Jesus) says *harmless as doves*, that is the kind of bearing he describes for the twelve as they go among wolves.
cards.prose: The dove in Noah's story came back in the evening with an olive leaf, and that told Noah the waters were going down. A dove carries news and does no harm. When Yahusha (Jesus) says *harmless as doves*, that is the kind of bearing he describes for the twelve as they go among wolves.
cards.member_note: Genesis 8:11 — *in her mouth was an olive leaf pluckt off: so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.* A dove brings Noah an olive leaf and the news that the waters are going down.

cards.src_text: Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be you therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.
cards.tgt_text: And Yahusha (Jesus), when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of Elohim (God) descending like a dove, and lighting upon him:
cards.old_note: The Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) descending in dove-form at the immersion — the dove-substance the disciples carry.
cards.note: Matthew 3:16 — *And Yahusha (Jesus), when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of Elohim (God) descending like a dove, and lighting upon him:* *Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be you therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.* (Matthew 10:16) At the Jordan the Spirit came down on Yahusha (Jesus) *like a dove*. cards.note: Mark 8:34 — *And when he had called the people unto him with his disciples also, he said unto them, Whosoever will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.* *And he that takes not his cross, and follows after me, is not worthy of me.* (Matthew 10:38) Mark shows who else was listening. He *called the people unto him with his disciples also*. In Matthew the saying is spoken to the twelve as they are sent, and in Mark the crowd is called in to hear it, so it was no secret of the inner circle.
cards.prose: Mark shows who else was listening. He *called the people unto him with his disciples also*. In Matthew the saying is spoken to the twelve as they are sent, and in Mark the crowd is called in to hear it, so it was no secret of the inner circle.
cards.member_note: Mark 8:34 — *let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.* Mark has him call the crowd in with his disciples to hear that anyone who follows must take up his cross.

cards.src_text: And he that takes not his cross, and follows after me, is not worthy of me.
cards.tgt_text: And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.
cards.old_note: The Lukan parallel with the *daily* element.
cards.note: Luke 9:23 — *And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.* *And he that takes not his cross, and follows after me, is not worthy of me.* (Matthew 10:38) Luke says it to *them all* and puts *daily* in front of the cross. What he tells the twelve at the sending is not one hour of courage but the way each day goes for the one who follows.
cards.prose: Luke says it to *them all* and puts *daily* in front of the cross. What he tells the twelve at the sending is not one hour of courage but the way each day goes for the one who follows.
cards.member_note: Luke 9:23 — *let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.* Luke adds that the cross is taken up daily, and says it to them all.

cards.src_text: And he that takes not his cross, and follows after me, is not worthy of me.
cards.tgt_text: And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.
cards.old_note: The further repetition with the cost-of-discipleship parables.
cards.note: Luke 14:27 — *And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.* *And he that takes not his cross, and follows after me, is not worthy of me.* (Matthew 10:38) Luke states the other side, as Matthew does at the end of the verse. Without the cross he says the man *cannot be my disciple*. It is a plain condition of following him, and Luke follows it at once with a man sitting down to count the cost.
cards.prose: Luke states the other side, as Matthew does at the end of the verse. Without the cross he says the man *cannot be my disciple*. It is a plain condition of following him, and Luke follows it at once with a man sitting down to count the cost.
cards.member_note: Luke 14:27 — *And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.* Luke says the one who does not bear his cross and come after him cannot be his disciple.

cards.src_text: He that finds his life shall lose it: and he that loses his life for my sake shall find it.
cards.tgt_text: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:
cards.old_note: The treasures-in-heaven framework — the kingdom-citizens' economic-orientation against the watcher-rebellion-administration's economic-orientation.
cards.note: Matthew 6:19 — *Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:* *He that finds his life shall lose it: and he that loses his life for my sake shall find it.* (Matthew 10:39) *He that findeth his life shall lose it.* The man who stores up for himself on earth has found his life in what moth and rust can eat. Yahusha (Jesus) told the crowd on the mountain the same, *treasures upon earth*, and finding and losing again turns on where the treasure is.
cards.prose: *He that findeth his life shall lose it.* The man who stores up for himself on earth has found his life in what moth and rust can eat. Yahusha (Jesus) told the crowd on the mountain the same, *treasures upon earth*, and finding and losing again turns on where the treasure is.
cards.member_note: Matthew 6:19 — *Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:* He tells the crowd not to lay up treasures on earth where moth and rust corrupt and thieves steal.

cards.src_text: He that finds his life shall lose it: and he that loses his life for my sake shall find it.
cards.tgt_text: Hear this, all ye people; give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world:
cards.old_note: The wisdom-tradition's reading that no man can redeem his brother's life and that wealth cannot bear a person through death.
cards.note: Psalm 49:1 — *Hear this, all ye people; give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world:* *He that finds his life shall lose it: and he that loses his life for my sake shall find it.* (Matthew 10:39) This psalm opens by calling *all ye people* to hear before it speaks of wisdom. What it goes on to speak of is the man who trusts in what he has gathered and the life that no riches can hold. His saying about finding a life and losing it is that old saying said again.
cards.prose: This psalm opens by calling *all ye people* to hear before it speaks of wisdom. What it goes on to speak of is the man who trusts in what he has gathered and the life that no riches can hold. His saying about finding a life and losing it is that old saying said again.
cards.member_note: Psalm 49:1 — *Hear this, all ye people; give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world:* The psalm opens by calling every person in the world to listen before it speaks of wisdom.

cards.src_text: He that receives you receives me, and he that receives me receives him that sent me.
cards.tgt_text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that receiveth whomsoever I send receiveth me; and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.
cards.old_note: *He that receiveth whomsoever I send receiveth me; and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me* — the parallel apostolic-representation pattern.
cards.note: John 13:20 — *Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that receiveth whomsoever I send receiveth me; and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.* *He that receives you receives me, and he that receives me receives him that sent me.* (Matthew 10:40) Matthew sets the chain of receiving at the sending out, and John sets it at the table later, in the same shape. Receive the one he sends and you receive him, and receive him and you receive *him that sent me*.
cards.prose: Matthew sets the chain of receiving at the sending out, and John sets it at the table later, in the same shape. Receive the one he sends and you receive him, and receive him and you receive *him that sent me*.
cards.member_note: John 13:20 — *Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that receiveth whomsoever I send receiveth me; and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.* John records the same chain: whoever receives the one he sends receives him, and whoever receives him receives the one who sent him.

cards.src_text: He that receives you receives me, and he that receives me receives him that sent me.
cards.tgt_text: And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
cards.old_note: *Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me* — the same representation-pattern at the eschatological-judgment.
cards.note: Matthew 25:40 — *And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.* *He that receives you receives me, and he that receives me receives him that sent me.* (Matthew 10:40) The same pattern is carried to the judgment. What is done for *the least of these my brethren* is counted as done for him. Here the receiving is traced to the end, so a welcome given to someone he sent is reckoned on the last day as given to him.
cards.prose: The same pattern is carried to the judgment. What is done for *the least of these my brethren* is counted as done for him. Here the receiving is traced to the end, so a welcome given to someone he sent is reckoned on the last day as given to him.
cards.member_note: Matthew 25:40 — *Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.* What is done to one of the least of his brethren he counts as done to himself.

cards.src_text: And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.
cards.tgt_text: Take heed that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise ye have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.
cards.old_note: The Pharisaic-grandstanding-religiosity the cup-of-cold-water economy inverts; the kingdom-economy operates at smallest-substance-given-with-right-heart, not at trumpet-blowing-with-public-display.
cards.note: Matthew 6:1 — *Take heed that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise ye have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.* *And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.* (Matthew 10:42) Set the cup of cold water beside alms given *to be seen of them*. One has no reward from the Father, and the other is only a drink of water in a disciple's name, and it will *in no wise lose* its reward. He weighs the gift by the heart behind it.
cards.prose: Set the cup of cold water beside alms given *to be seen of them*. One has no reward from the Father, and the other is only a drink of water in a disciple's name, and it will *in no wise lose* its reward. He weighs the gift by the heart behind it.
cards.member_note: Matthew 6:1 — *to be seen of them: otherwise ye have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.* Alms given before men to be seen have no reward from the Father, the opposite of the cup of water given quietly.

cards.src_text: And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.
cards.tgt_text: Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:
cards.old_note: *Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:* (Matthew 25:34). At the sifting of the sheep from the goats, the cup of cold water given to *one of these little ones* (Matthew 10:42) becomes the *inasmuch as ye have done it* the King remembers.
cards.note: Matthew 25:34 — *Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:* *And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.* (Matthew 10:42) The reward that shall not be lost has a place at the end of the road, a kingdom *prepared for you from the foundation of the world*. The King calls those on his right hand *ye blessed of my Father*. The cup of water is not the price of that kingdom. It is one of the small things he does not let drop.
cards.prose: The reward that shall not be lost has a place at the end of the road, a kingdom *prepared for you from the foundation of the world*. The King calls those on his right hand *ye blessed of my Father*. The cup of water is not the price of that kingdom. It is one of the small things he does not let drop.
cards.member_note: Matthew 25:34 — *Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.* At the judgment the King calls the sheep blessed and gives them the kingdom prepared from the foundation of the world.

cards.src_text: Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
cards.tgt_text: Thus saith Yahuah (LORD), Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls. But they said, We will not walk therein.
cards.old_note: *Ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls* — the direct Tanakh-citation.
cards.note: Jeremiah 6:16 — *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD), Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls. But they said, We will not walk therein.* *Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.* (Matthew 11:28) Yahusha (Jesus) says *I will give you rest* to the weary, and Jeremiah shows where Yahuah (the LORD) has always said rest is found, on the old paths, the good way, walked. The invitation sends the tired back onto the road the Father laid out, and the sorrow at the end of Jeremiah's verse, *We will not walk therein*, is the refusal the weary are being called out of.
cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says *I will give you rest* to the weary, and Jeremiah shows where Yahuah (the LORD) has always said rest is found, on the old paths, the good way, walked. The invitation sends the tired back onto the road the Father laid out, and the sorrow at the end of Jeremiah's verse, *We will not walk therein*, is the refusal the weary are being called out of.
cards.member_note: Jeremiah 6:16 — *ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls.* Yahuah (the LORD) sets the rest at the end of a walk on the old paths, the good way, and records that the people refused it.

cards.src_text: Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
cards.tgt_text: To whom he said, This is the rest wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest; and this is the refreshing: yet they would not hear.
cards.old_note: *This is the rest wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest.*
cards.note: Isaiah 28:12 — *To whom he said, This is the rest wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest; and this is the refreshing: yet they would not hear.* *Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.* (Matthew 11:28) The rest offered to those who *labour and are heavy laden* was already being held out in Isaiah to a weary people, and Isaiah's verse closes the way Jeremiah's does, with *they would not hear*. The same refusal runs through both, and it is into that refusal that a man now stands and says come.
cards.prose: The rest offered to those who *labour and are heavy laden* was already being held out in Isaiah to a weary people, and Isaiah's verse closes the way Jeremiah's does, with *they would not hear*. The same refusal runs through both, and it is into that refusal that a man now stands and says come.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 28:12 — *To whom he said, This is the rest wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest; and this is the refreshing: yet they would not hear.* Isaiah names the rest that eases the weary and says plainly that the people would not hear it.

cards.src_text: Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
cards.tgt_text: For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.
cards.old_note: The Pharisaic-burden the King's-yoke contrasts against.
cards.note: Matthew 23:4 — *For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.* *Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.* (Matthew 11:28) The ones who *labour and are heavy laden* are not bent under the Father's commandments. The load Yahusha (Jesus) names elsewhere is the one the scribes and Pharisees lay on, where they *bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne* and set them on men's shoulders, and will not lift a finger to move them. The people under that load are the ones he calls to himself.
cards.prose: The ones who *labour and are heavy laden* are not bent under the Father's commandments. The load Yahusha (Jesus) names elsewhere is the one the scribes and Pharisees lay on, where they *bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne* and set them on men's shoulders, and will not lift a finger to move them. The people under that load are the ones he calls to himself.
cards.member_note: Matthew 23:4 — *they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders.* Yahusha (Jesus) names the heavy, grievous load that was bound on the people's shoulders, the weight the weary are called out from.

cards.src_text: Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
cards.tgt_text: Now therefore why tempt ye Elohim (God), to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
cards.old_note: Kefa's (Peter's) apostolic-restatement.
cards.note: Acts 15:10 — *Now therefore why tempt ye Elohim (God), to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?* *Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.* (Matthew 11:28) Peter speaks of a yoke too, one laid on the neck of the disciples *which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear*. The fathers walked the Father's commandments, so this cannot be them. It is the demand pressed on people whose hearts the Father had already cleansed, that they be made something before they were counted in, and it is that weight the call to rest answers.
cards.prose: Peter speaks of a yoke too, one laid on the neck of the disciples *which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear*. The fathers walked the Father's commandments, so this cannot be them. It is the demand pressed on people whose hearts the Father had already cleansed, that they be made something before they were counted in, and it is that weight the call to rest answers.
cards.member_note: Acts 15:10 — *to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear.* Peter names a yoke on the disciples' necks that neither the fathers nor he could bear, the kind of load Yahusha's (Jesus's) call to the weary lifts off.

cards.src_text: Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
cards.tgt_text: And profited in the Yahudim's (Jews’) religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers.
cards.old_note: *The traditions of my fathers* — Paul naming the Pharisaic-oral-tradition the kingdom-citizens are released from.
cards.note: Galatians 1:14 — *And profited in the Yahudim's (Jews’) religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers.* *Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.* (Matthew 11:28) Paul tells what he carried before he was called, a zeal for *the traditions of my fathers* that put him ahead of many his own age. That is the human weight laid over the commandments, and it is the sort of burden the weary are told to bring to Yahusha (Jesus). It was never the instruction Moses gave that wore them out.
cards.prose: Paul tells what he carried before he was called, a zeal for *the traditions of my fathers* that put him ahead of many his own age. That is the human weight laid over the commandments, and it is the sort of burden the weary are told to bring to Yahusha (Jesus). It was never the instruction Moses gave that wore them out.
cards.member_note: Galatians 1:14 — *being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers.* Paul names the handed-down traditions he was once zealous for, the human weight laid over the commandments that the weary are called out from.

cards.src_text: Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
cards.tgt_text: But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, saith Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.
cards.old_note: The Torah-on-the-heart Tanakh-anchor — the substance of the King's-yoke.
cards.note: Jeremiah 31:33 — *But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, saith Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.* *Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.* (Matthew 11:28) The rest he promises here is not rest apart from the commandment. This is the covenant word to the house of Yashar'el (Israel), that Yahuah (the LORD) would put his law in their inward parts and *write it in their hearts*. What weighs on the weary is what men added, and what he gives is the commandment set back where it was always meant to live.
cards.prose: The rest he promises here is not rest apart from the commandment. This is the covenant word to the house of Yashar'el (Israel), that Yahuah (the LORD) would put his law in their inward parts and *write it in their hearts*. What weighs on the weary is what men added, and what he gives is the commandment set back where it was always meant to live.
cards.member_note: Jeremiah 31:33 — *I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts.* The covenant promise to the house of Yashar'el (Israel) is the law written in the heart, not set aside, and the rest he offers goes with it.

cards.src_text: Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
cards.tgt_text: A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.
cards.old_note: The new-heart-and-new-spirit Tanakh-promise — the substance that makes the yoke easy.
cards.note: Ezekiel 36:26 — *A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.* *Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.* (Matthew 11:28) A man can put down a load, but he cannot take a stony heart out of his own chest. Here the Father says he will do it himself and give *an heart of flesh*. This is what makes the commandment light to carry, and the rest on offer rides on that promise.
cards.prose: A man can put down a load, but he cannot take a stony heart out of his own chest. Here the Father says he will do it himself and give *an heart of flesh*. This is what makes the commandment light to carry, and the rest on offer rides on that promise.
cards.member_note: Ezekiel 36:26 — *I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.* Yahuah (the LORD) promises to take out the stony heart and give a heart of flesh, which is what makes his way light to carry.

cards.src_text: Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
cards.tgt_text: For this is the love of Elohim (God), that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.
cards.old_note: *His commandments are not grievous.*
cards.note: 1 John 5:3 — *For this is the love of Elohim (God), that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.* *Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.* (Matthew 11:28) John sets the weary beside the commandments themselves. Keeping them is the love of Elohim (God), and they are *not grievous*. So the weight on the weary was never the commandments, and the one who says come and rest is calling them toward the keeping, not away from it.
cards.prose: John sets the weary beside the commandments themselves. Keeping them is the love of Elohim (God), and they are *not grievous*. So the weight on the weary was never the commandments, and the one who says come and rest is calling them toward the keeping, not away from it.
cards.member_note: 1 John 5:3 — *For this is the love of Elohim (God), that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.* John says plainly that keeping the commandments is the love of Elohim (God) and that they are not grievous.

cards.src_text: Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
cards.tgt_text: Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.
cards.old_note: The load-bearing anti-antinomian declaration of the Sermon — the Torah Yahusha (Jesus) is yoking the disciples to is the Father's-Torah-internalized.
cards.note: Matthew 5:17 — *Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.* *Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.* (Matthew 11:28) Nobody should hear *I will give you rest* as a man putting the law down. The same Yahusha (Jesus) says he is *not come to destroy, but to fulfil*, and the two together show the rest is found with the commandments standing, not with them taken away.
cards.prose: Nobody should hear *I will give you rest* as a man putting the law down. The same Yahusha (Jesus) says he is *not come to destroy, but to fulfil*, and the two together show the rest is found with the commandments standing, not with them taken away.
cards.member_note: Matthew 5:17 — *Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.* Yahusha (Jesus) says he did not come to destroy the law or the prophets, so the rest he gives is not a release from the Torah.

cards.src_text: All things are delivered unto me of my Father: and no man knows the Son, but the Father; neither knows any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.
cards.tgt_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.
cards.old_note: *All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth* — the post-resurrection restatement of the *all things delivered* substance.
cards.note: Matthew 28:18 — *And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* *All things are delivered unto me of my Father: and no man knows the Son, but the Father; neither knows any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.* (Matthew 11:27) *All things are delivered unto me of my Father* is said here before the cross, and after the tomb he says it again as all power given. In both the one who gives is the Father and the one who receives is the Son. The authority was never something the Son took.
cards.prose: *All things are delivered unto me of my Father* is said here before the cross, and after the tomb he says it again as all power given. In both the one who gives is the Father and the one who receives is the Son. The authority was never something the Son took.
cards.member_note: Matthew 28:18 — *And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* After the resurrection the Son says again that all power has been given to him, the same handing over by the Father.

cards.src_text: All things are delivered unto me of my Father: and no man knows the Son, but the Father; neither knows any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.
cards.tgt_text: No man hath seen Elohim (God) at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him.
cards.old_note: *No man hath seen Elohim (God) at any time; the only begotten Son ... he hath declared him* — the parallel revelation-economy statement.
cards.note: John 1:18 — *No man hath seen Elohim (God) at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him.* *All things are delivered unto me of my Father: and no man knows the Son, but the Father; neither knows any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.* (Matthew 11:27) Matthew has the Son saying *neither knoweth any man the Father, save the Son*, and John says it from the other side. The Father is unseen, and the Son, who is in his bosom, is the one who has made him known. The one who can be seen is the one who shows the one who cannot.
cards.prose: Matthew has the Son saying *neither knoweth any man the Father, save the Son*, and John says it from the other side. The Father is unseen, and the Son, who is in his bosom, is the one who has made him known. The one who can be seen is the one who shows the one who cannot.
cards.member_note: John 1:18 — *No man hath seen Elohim (God) at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him.* No man has seen the Father, and the only begotten Son, who is in his bosom, is the one who has declared him.

cards.src_text: All things are delivered unto me of my Father: and no man knows the Son, but the Father; neither knows any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.
cards.tgt_text: Then answered Yahusha (Jesus) and said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do: for what things soever he doeth, these also doeth the Son likewise.
cards.old_note: *The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do* — the Son's-derived-substance from the Father.
cards.note: John 5:19 — *Then answered Yahusha (Jesus) and said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do: for what things soever he doeth, these also doeth the Son likewise.* *All things are delivered unto me of my Father: and no man knows the Son, but the Father; neither knows any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.* (Matthew 11:27) The Father handing all things to the Son is not the Son acting on his own. John has it from the Son's own mouth, that he does only *what he seeth the Father do*. What the Father gives is what the Son carries out, and that is how he can make the Father known to whomever he will.

cards.old_note: *He that hath seen me hath seen the Father* — the Son-reveals-the-Father substance.
cards.note: John 14:6 — *Yahusha (Jesus) saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.* *All things are delivered unto me of my Father: and no man knows the Son, but the Father; neither knows any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.* (Matthew 11:27) Matthew says no one knows the Father except the Son and the one the Son chooses to show him. John puts the same thing as a road, *no man cometh unto the Father, but by me*. The Father is the one to be reached, and the Son is the one who opens the way and leads there.

cards.old_note: *To us there is but one Elohim (God), the Father ... and one Lord Yahusha (Jesus) Messiah (Christ), by whom are all things* — Paul's Father-Son framework statement.
cards.note: 1 Corinthians 8:6 — *But to us there is but one Elohim (God), the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Lord Jesus Christ), by whom are all things, and we by him.* *All things are delivered unto me of my Father: and no man knows the Son, but the Father; neither knows any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.* (Matthew 11:27) Paul holds the two apart and together. That is Matthew's order, the Father as the source who delivers, and the Son as the one through whom it is known and done.

cards.note: Colossians 1:15 — *Who is the image of the invisible Elohim (God), the firstborn of every creature:* *All things are delivered unto me of my Father: and no man knows the Son, but the Father; neither knows any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.* (Matthew 11:27) The Father is unseen and without form, and Paul says the Son is *the image of the invisible Elohim (God)*. cards.src_text: The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.
cards.tgt_text: And there was delivered unto him the book of the prophet Esaias. And when he had opened the book, he found the place where it was written,
cards.old_note: The Nazareth-synagogue reading where Yahusha (Jesus) closes the scroll mid-verse, omitting the same day-of-vengeance clause.
cards.note: Luke 4:17 — *And there was delivered unto him the book of the prophet Esaias. And when he had opened the book, he found the place where it was written,* *The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.* (Matthew 11:5) What Yahusha (Jesus) tells John's men to report is out of Isaiah, and at Nazareth he is handed that same book and finds the place. He reads *recovering of sight to the blind* (Luke 4:18), stops at *the acceptable year of Yahuah (Lord)* (Luke 4:19), and closes the scroll, leaving off the day of vengeance that Isaiah's next words name. The works John hears about are the first half of that reading.

He answers *Elias truly shall first come, and restore all things* (Matthew 17:11), and then *the disciples understood that he spake unto them of John the Baptist* (Matthew 17:13).

cards.src_text: Woe unto you, Chorazin! woe unto you, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.

cards.note: Ezekiel 28:1 — *The word of Yahuah (LORD) came again unto me, saying,* *Woe unto you, Chorazin! woe unto you, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.* (Matthew 11:21) Yahusha (Jesus) names Tyre and Sidon as cities that would have repented in sackcloth and ashes at the works done in Chorazin. It is a city under a word of judgment, and still it is counted better off than the towns that saw him.

cards.note: John 10:14 — *I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine.* *At that time Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, I thank you, O Father, Yahuah (Lord) of heaven and earth, because you have hid these things from the wise and prudent, and have revealed them unto babes.* (Matthew 11:25) The Father hides from the wise and *hast revealed them unto babes*, and the Son says he knows his sheep and is known of them. cards.src_text: At that time Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, I thank you, O Father, Yahuah (Lord) of heaven and earth, because you have hid these things from the wise and prudent, and have revealed them unto babes.
cards.tgt_text: For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of Elohim (God).
cards.old_note: *Hath not Elohim (God) made foolish the wisdom of this world? ... Elohim (God) hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise* — Paul's restatement of the babes-over-wise revelation-economy.
cards.note: 1 Corinthians 1:18 — *For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of Elohim (God).* *At that time Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, I thank you, O Father, Yahuah (Lord) of heaven and earth, because you have hid these things from the wise and prudent, and have revealed them unto babes.* (Matthew 11:25) Paul sees the same dividing line. cards.src_text: But he said unto them, Have you not read what David did, when he was an hungred, and they that were with him;
cards.tgt_text: Then came David to Nob to Ahimelech the priest: and Ahimelech was afraid at the meeting of David, and said unto him, Why art thou alone, and no man with thee?
cards.old_note: David and the showbread Tanakh-precedent.
cards.note: 1 Samuel 21:1 — *Then came David to Nob to Ahimelech the priest: and Ahimelech was afraid at the meeting of David, and said unto him, Why art thou alone, and no man with thee?* *But he said unto them, Have you not read what David did, when he was an hungred, and they that were with him;* (Matthew 12:3) *Have ye not read what David did*, he asks, and the reading starts here. David comes to Nob, the priest is afraid at the sight of him, and the only bread to be had is the bread set apart for the priests. Nothing in the story calls it a sin, so Yahusha (Jesus) is not loosening the rule about the holy bread, he is reading it the way it was written.

cards.src_text: Or have you not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless?
cards.tgt_text: Every sabbath he shall set it in order before Yahuah (LORD) continually, being taken from the children of Yashar'el (Israel) by an everlasting covenant.
cards.old_note: The showbread-replacement on Shabbat — Torah-mandated work.
cards.note: Leviticus 24:8 — *Every sabbath he shall set it in order before Yahuah (LORD) continually, being taken from the children of Yashar'el (Israel) by an everlasting covenant.* *Or have you not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless?* (Matthew 12:5) The Torah itself gives the priests a task for every sabbath, and the verse says so plainly: *Every sabbath he shall set it in order*. So when Yahusha (Jesus) says the priests in the temple *profane the sabbath, and are blameless*, he is not pointing at a loophole. He is pointing at work the commandment itself calls for, and it is the very bread David ate.

cards.member_note: Leviticus 24:8 — *Every sabbath he shall set it in order before Yahuah (LORD) continually, being taken from the children of Yashar'el (Israel) by an everlasting covenant.* The bread was set in order before Yahuah (the LORD) every sabbath by an everlasting covenant, so sabbath work was commanded in the Torah itself.

cards.src_text: For the Son of Adam is the Lord even of the sabbath day.
cards.tgt_text: And Elohim (God) blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which Elohim (God) created and made.
cards.old_note: The Shabbat-sanctification at creation.
cards.note: Genesis 2:3 — *And Elohim (God) blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which Elohim (God) created and made.* *For the Son of Adam is the Lord even of the sabbath day.* (Matthew 12:8) The one who is *Adonai (Lord) even of the sabbath day* is claiming a day, not cancelling one, and Genesis shows whose day it was. Elohim (God) blessed the seventh day and made it holy at the very start, before there was a Pharisee or a fence or a priest, so the Son of Adam is master of a day that was holy before any man laid a rule on it.

cards.member_note: Genesis 2:3 — *blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it.* Elohim (God) blessed the seventh day and made it holy at creation, so the day Yahusha (Jesus) is master of was set apart before any man's rule.

cards.src_text: For the Son of Adam is the Lord even of the sabbath day.
cards.tgt_text: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.
cards.old_note: The Decalogue's-Shabbat-command — the Torah-substance the King is restoring.
cards.note: Exodus 20:8 — *Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.* *For the Son of Adam is the Lord even of the sabbath day.* (Matthew 12:8) This is the commandment he stands as master over, and nothing he says to the Pharisees sets it down. He is clearing off what men stacked on top of it so that *to keep it holy* can be heard plainly again, and he does it as the one whose voice spoke it in the first place.

cards.member_note: Exodus 20:8 — *Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.* The commandment itself, the plain word to remember the sabbath day and keep it holy, which Yahusha (Jesus) stands behind and never sets down.

cards.src_text: And when he was departed thence, he went into their synagogue:
cards.tgt_text: Moses therefore gave unto you circumcision; (not because it is of Moses, but of the fathers;) and ye on the sabbath day circumcise a man.
cards.old_note: Yahusha (Jesus) again deploying the same circumcision-on-Shabbat argument later in the gospel.
cards.note: John 7:22 — *Moses therefore gave unto you circumcision; (not because it is of Moses, but of the fathers;) and ye on the sabbath day circumcise a man.* *And when he was departed thence, he went into their synagogue:* (Matthew 12:9) They ask in the synagogue whether it is lawful to heal on the sabbath, and later in John he answers from their own practice. They circumcise a man on the sabbath so the law of Moses will not be broken, and then they are angry that he *made a man every whit whole on the sabbath day* (John 7:23). If one commandment can be kept on the day of the other, healing is no breach.

cards.src_text: How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.
cards.tgt_text: If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of Yahuah (LORD), honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words:
cards.old_note: *If thou turn away thy foot from the Shabbat ... and call the Shabbat a delight* — the Tanakh-substance of Shabbat-as-delight.
cards.note: Isaiah 58:13 — *If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of Yahuah (LORD), honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words:* *How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.* (Matthew 12:12) He closes the matter with *it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days*, and Isaiah shows that is no softening of the day. The prophet calls the sabbath a delight, set apart from doing our own ways, and lifting a man out of his trouble is that delight itself rather than a breach of the day.

cards.src_text: At that time Yahusha (Jesus) went on the sabbath day through the corn; and his disciples were an hungred, and began to pluck the ears of corn, and to eat.
cards.tgt_text: There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of Elohim (God).
cards.old_note: *There remaineth therefore a rest (*sabbatismos* — Shabbat-keeping) to the people of Elohim (God)* — the apostolic-affirmation.
cards.note: Hebrews 4:9 — *There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of Elohim (God).* *At that time Yahusha (Jesus) went on the sabbath day through the corn; and his disciples were an hungred, and began to pluck the ears of corn, and to eat.* (Matthew 12:1) The disciples walk through the field on the sabbath day with their master, and Hebrews shows the day did not stop there. A rest still *remaineth* for the people of Elohim (God), and the next verse says what that rest is: whoever has entered it has *ceased from his own works, as Elohim (God) did from his* (Hebrews 4:10). That is the seventh day's rest, still standing.

cards.src_text: At that time Yahusha (Jesus) went on the sabbath day through the corn; and his disciples were an hungred, and began to pluck the ears of corn, and to eat.
cards.tgt_text: And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them, and three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures,
cards.old_note: Paul's-Shabbat-keeping pattern in his missionary journeys.
cards.note: Acts 17:2 — *And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them, and three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures,* *At that time Yahusha (Jesus) went on the sabbath day through the corn; and his disciples were an hungred, and began to pluck the ears of corn, and to eat.* (Matthew 12:1) The disciples walk through the corn on the sabbath day with their master, and that is the pattern Acts carries forward. Paul went into the synagogue *as his manner was*, and for three weeks he reasoned from the scriptures on the sabbath, which is not what a man does who thinks the day has been taken away.

cards.src_text: At that time Yahusha (Jesus) went on the sabbath day through the corn; and his disciples were an hungred, and began to pluck the ears of corn, and to eat.
cards.tgt_text: And he shall speak great words against the El Elyon (most High), and shall wear out the saints of the El Elyon (most High), and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time.
cards.old_note: *Think to change times and laws* — the institutional-Christian-Sunday-Law as the antichrist-system's Daniel 7:25 substance; the framework rules out the institutional-Christian-claim that the King abolished the Shabbat.
cards.note: Daniel 7:25 — *And he shall speak great words against the El Elyon (most High), and shall wear out the saints of the El Elyon (most High), and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time.* *At that time Yahusha (Jesus) went on the sabbath day through the corn; and his disciples were an hungred, and began to pluck the ears of corn, and to eat.* (Matthew 12:1) He walked through that field as a keeper of the day, answering men who had piled their own rules on it and never touching the commandment underneath. Daniel gives the changing of the times to another figure, the king who rises up after the ten kings and shall *think to change times and laws*. A teaching that makes the Son of Adam the one who ended the sabbath has put on him what Daniel says of that king.

cards.src_text: Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) shall not be forgiven unto men.
cards.tgt_text: But the Pharisees said, He casteth out devils through the prince of the devils.
cards.old_note: The first appearance of the Beelzebul-attribution; the trajectory begins.
cards.note: Matthew 9:34 — *But the Pharisees said, He casteth out devils through the prince of the devils.* *Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) shall not be forgiven unto men.* (Matthew 12:31) This is not the first time the charge is thrown. Earlier in Matthew, when the dumb man spoke, the Pharisees said he casts out devils through *the prince of the devils*, and he let it stand. Here he answers it, and the answer is that what they call devilish is the Spirit's work, which is why he speaks of *blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit)* right here.

cards.src_text: Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) shall not be forgiven unto men.
cards.tgt_text: It is enough for the disciple that he be as his master, and the servant as his lord. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, how much more shall they call them of his household?
cards.old_note: The Beelzebul-attribution extended to the household; the trajectory continues.
cards.note: Matthew 10:25 — *It is enough for the disciple that he be as his master, and the servant as his lord. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, how much more shall they call them of his household?* *Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) shall not be forgiven unto men.* (Matthew 12:31) He told the twelve this would come. If the master of the house was called Beelzebub, those of his household would be called the same and worse, so the name put on him here is the name his disciples were told to expect. The accusation is a plain one, and the saying about the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) falls on those who see what the work is and still call it devilish.

cards.src_text: Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) shall not be forgiven unto men.
cards.tgt_text: Verily I say unto you, All sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme:
cards.old_note: The Markan parallel with the explanatory clarification.
cards.note: Mark 3:28 — *Verily I say unto you, All sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme:* *Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) shall not be forgiven unto men.* (Matthew 12:31) Mark opens with the wide mercy, that all sins and blasphemies shall be forgiven to the sons of men, and Matthew sets the same words beside the exception. Mark then says why the exception is there: *Because they said, He hath an unclean spirit* (Mark 3:30). The line falls where the Spirit's work is named unclean.

cards.src_text: Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) shall not be forgiven unto men.
cards.tgt_text: And whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of Adam, it shall be forgiven him: but unto him that blasphemeth against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) it shall not be forgiven.
cards.old_note: The Lukan parallel.
cards.note: Luke 12:10 — *And whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of Adam, it shall be forgiven him: but unto him that blasphemeth against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) it shall not be forgiven.* *Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) shall not be forgiven unto men.* (Matthew 12:31) Luke sets the saying among confessing and denying him before men, so it sits with the question of who stands with him and who stands against. A *word against the Son of Adam* is forgiven again, and the one who *blasphemeth against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit)* is not, which tells us the line runs at the Spirit's work and not at a man's slowness to see who he is.
