cards.tgt_text: But though he had done so many miracles before them, yet they believed not on him:
cards.old_note: Yochanan's (John's) application of the same citation.
cards.note: John 12:37 — *But though he had done so many miracles before them, yet they believed not on him:* *Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.* (Matthew 13:13) He speaks in parables because they see and do not see. John says what that looked like in the crowd. After so many miracles *they believed not on him*. Seeing the works without seeing him is exactly what the parable-speech describes.
cards.prose: He speaks in parables because they see and do not see. John says what that looked like in the crowd. After so many miracles *they believed not on him*. Seeing the works without seeing him is exactly what the parable-speech describes.
cards.member_note: John 12:37 — *But though he had done so many miracles before them, yet they believed not on him:* Though he had done so many miracles before them, they believed not on him.

cards.src_text: Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.
cards.tgt_text: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spake the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers,
cards.old_note: Paul's application in Rome.
cards.note: Acts 28:25 — *And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spake the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers,* *Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.* (Matthew 13:13) They see and do not see, hear and do not understand. At Rome Paul puts a name to the one who first said it: the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) spoke it through Isaiah to the fathers. It is an old word about this people, not a new charge, and the hearers there parted ways over it.
cards.prose: They see and do not see, hear and do not understand. At Rome Paul puts a name to the one who first said it: the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) spoke it through Isaiah to the fathers. It is an old word about this people, not a new charge, and the hearers there parted ways over it.
cards.member_note: Acts 28:25 — *Well spake the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers.* Paul at Rome says the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) spoke the word about seeing without perceiving by Isaiah to the fathers.

cards.src_text: Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.
cards.tgt_text: What then? Yashar'el (Israel) hath not obtained that which he seeketh for; but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded
cards.old_note: The same diagnostic in Paul's olive-tree exposition.
cards.note: Romans 11:7 — *What then? Yashar'el (Israel) hath not obtained that which he seeketh for; but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded* *Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.* (Matthew 13:13) Seeing they see not describes Yashar'el (Israel) when Paul wrote. The house sought what it did not obtain, and *the election hath obtained it*, while the rest were blinded. Those who do not understand the parables are the rest. Those who do were the election before the telling.
cards.prose: Seeing they see not describes Yashar'el (Israel) when Paul wrote. The house sought what it did not obtain, and *the election hath obtained it*, while the rest were blinded. Those who do not understand the parables are the rest. Those who do were the election before the telling.
cards.member_note: Romans 11:7 — *but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded.* The election obtained what Yashar'el (Israel) sought, and the rest were blinded.

cards.src_text: Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:
cards.tgt_text: Then Yahusha (Jesus) sent the multitude away, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field.
cards.old_note: The King's-own-interpretation.
cards.note: Matthew 13:36 — *Then Yahusha (Jesus) sent the multitude away, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field.* *Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:* (Matthew 13:24) He gave the crowd the story of the good seed and the field. In the house the disciples ask him to declare it, *the parable of the tares of the field*. What the crowd got as a picture the disciples get as a plain account, one piece at a time.
cards.prose: He gave the crowd the story of the good seed and the field. In the house the disciples ask him to declare it, *the parable of the tares of the field*. What the crowd got as a picture the disciples get as a plain account, one piece at a time.
cards.member_note: Matthew 13:36 — *Then Yahusha (Jesus) sent the multitude away, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field.* The disciples ask him in the house to declare the parable of the tares, and he gives them the plain account.

cards.src_text: Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:
cards.tgt_text: And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them,
cards.old_note: The fallen-angels' incursion bringing the giants.
cards.note: Genesis 6:1 — *And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them,* *Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:* (Matthew 13:24) The man sowed good seed in his field. Genesis shows the field filling: *when men began to multiply on the face of the earth*. Into that earth came the sons of Elohim (God), who *came in unto the daughters of men* (Genesis 6:4). The enemy's seed went in among the good.
cards.prose: The man sowed good seed in his field. Genesis shows the field filling: *when men began to multiply on the face of the earth*. Into that earth came the sons of Elohim (God), who *came in unto the daughters of men* (Genesis 6:4). The enemy's seed went in among the good.
cards.member_note: Genesis 6:1 — *And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them,* Men multiplied on the earth and daughters were born, the field the good seed was sown in.

cards.src_text: Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:
cards.tgt_text: Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath Elohim (God) said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?
cards.old_note: The serpent's-corruption of the line; the seed-war foretold.
cards.note: Genesis 3:1 — *Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath Elohim (God) said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?* *Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:* (Matthew 13:24) Good seed is sown first in the householder's field, and the trouble comes by a voice that talks. The serpent comes to the woman in the garden and puts the sower's own word in doubt. The enemy of the parable begins by making the word look like something that might not have been said.
cards.prose: Good seed is sown first in the householder's field, and the trouble comes by a voice that talks. The serpent comes to the woman in the garden and puts the sower's own word in doubt. The enemy of the parable begins by making the word look like something that might not have been said.
cards.member_note: Genesis 3:1 — *And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath Elohim (God) said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?* The serpent asks the woman whether Elohim (God) really said it, the enemy's first move against the sown word.

cards.src_text: Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field:
cards.tgt_text: Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); I will also take of the highest branch of the high cedar, and will set it; I will crop off from the top of his young twigs a tender one, and will plant it upon an high mountain and eminent:
cards.old_note: The Messianic-tree imagery with the birds-of-the-air lodging.
cards.note: Ezekiel 17:22 — *Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); I will also take of the highest branch of the high cedar, and will set it; I will crop off from the top of his young twigs a tender one, and will plant it upon an high mountain and eminent:* *Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field:* (Matthew 13:31) A small seed grows into a tree where the birds of the air lodge, and Yahuah (the LORD) says he will crop a tender twig from the top of the cedar and plant it on a high mountain. The next verse names the place: *In the mountain of the height of Yashar'el (Israel) will I plant it* (Ezekiel 17:23). The little beginning is something he plants himself.
cards.prose: A small seed grows into a tree where the birds of the air lodge, and Yahuah (the LORD) says he will crop a tender twig from the top of the cedar and plant it on a high mountain. The next verse names the place: *In the mountain of the height of Yashar'el (Israel) will I plant it* (Ezekiel 17:23). The little beginning is something he plants himself.
cards.member_note: Ezekiel 17:22 — *I will crop off from the top of his young twigs a tender one, and will plant it upon an high mountain and eminent.* Yahuah (the LORD) takes a tender twig and plants it on the high mountain of Yashar'el (Israel), where it becomes a great tree.

cards.src_text: Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field:
cards.tgt_text: The leaves thereof were fair, and the fruit thereof much, and in it was meat for all: the beasts of the field had shadow under it, and the fowls of the heaven dwelt in the boughs thereof, and all flesh was fed of it.
cards.old_note: Nebuchadnezzar's kingdom-tree imagery.
cards.note: Daniel 4:12 — *The leaves thereof were fair, and the fruit thereof much, and in it was meat for all: the beasts of the field had shadow under it, and the fowls of the heaven dwelt in the boughs thereof, and all flesh was fed of it.* *Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field:* (Matthew 13:31) A tree with *the fowls of the heaven* in its boughs is how Daniel's page draws a kingdom. This one stood in the midst of the earth with food for all flesh until a watcher came down and called for it to be hewn. The mustard tree is set among the same pictures.
cards.prose: A tree with *the fowls of the heaven* in its boughs is how Daniel's page draws a kingdom. This one stood in the midst of the earth with food for all flesh until a watcher came down and called for it to be hewn. The mustard tree is set among the same pictures.
cards.member_note: Daniel 4:12 — *the beasts of the field had shadow under it, and the fowls of the heaven dwelt in the boughs thereof, and all flesh was fed of it.* Nebuchadnezzar's great tree shelters the beasts and the fowls of heaven and feeds all flesh, the picture of a kingdom.

cards.src_text: Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field:
cards.tgt_text: All the fowls of heaven made their nests in his boughs, and under his branches did all the beasts of the field bring forth their young, and under his shadow dwelt all great nations.
cards.old_note: The cedar-of-Lebanon kingdom-tree with the birds-of-the-air nesting.
cards.note: Ezekiel 31:6 — *All the fowls of heaven made their nests in his boughs, and under his branches did all the beasts of the field bring forth their young, and under his shadow dwelt all great nations.* *Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field:* (Matthew 13:31) Ezekiel's great tree had *all the fowls of heaven* nesting in its boughs, and under its shadow *dwelt all great nations*. That is how a grown kingdom is drawn. When the least of seeds becomes a tree with birds in its branches, the listener already has these pictures in mind.
cards.prose: Ezekiel's great tree had *all the fowls of heaven* nesting in its boughs, and under its shadow *dwelt all great nations*. That is how a grown kingdom is drawn. When the least of seeds becomes a tree with birds in its branches, the listener already has these pictures in mind.
cards.member_note: Ezekiel 31:6 — *All the fowls of heaven made their nests in his boughs, and under his branches did all the beasts of the field bring forth their young, and under his shadow dwelt all great nations.* Ezekiel's great tree has the fowls of heaven nesting in its boughs and great nations dwelling in its shadow.

cards.src_text: All these things spake Yahusha (Jesus) unto the multitude in parables; and without a parable spake he not unto them:
cards.tgt_text: I will open my mouth in a parable: I will utter dark sayings of old:
cards.old_note: Direct Tanakh-source.
cards.note: Psalm 78:2 — *I will open my mouth in a parable: I will utter dark sayings of old:* *All these things spake Yahusha (Jesus) unto the multitude in parables; and without a parable spake he not unto them:* (Matthew 13:34) He spoke to the crowd only in parables, and this is the psalm being filled. The psalmist opens his mouth in a parable and utters *dark sayings of old*. What Yahusha (Jesus) says by the sea is not new speech. It is the old dark saying handed to the fathers' children, now spoken aloud.
cards.prose: He spoke to the crowd only in parables, and this is the psalm being filled. The psalmist opens his mouth in a parable and utters *dark sayings of old*. What Yahusha (Jesus) says by the sea is not new speech. It is the old dark saying handed to the fathers' children, now spoken aloud.
cards.member_note: Psalm 78:2 — *I will open my mouth in a parable: I will utter dark sayings of old:* The psalmist opens his mouth in a parable and utters dark sayings of old, the word Yahusha (Jesus) takes up.

cards.src_text: All these things spake Yahusha (Jesus) unto the multitude in parables; and without a parable spake he not unto them:
cards.tgt_text: Now to him that is of power to stablish you according to my gospel, and the preaching of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ), according to the revelation of the mystery, which was kept secret since the world began,
cards.old_note: The mystery-kept-secret-since-the-world-began now made manifest.
cards.note: Romans 16:25 — *Now to him that is of power to stablish you according to my gospel, and the preaching of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ), according to the revelation of the mystery, which was kept secret since the world began,* *All these things spake Yahusha (Jesus) unto the multitude in parables; and without a parable spake he not unto them:* (Matthew 13:34) Paul speaks of a mystery *kept secret since the world began*, and then says it *is made manifest, and by the scriptures of the prophets* (Romans 16:26). What Yahusha (Jesus) says only in parables is that same hidden thing, and it was never apart from the prophets.
cards.prose: Paul speaks of a mystery *kept secret since the world began*, and then says it *is made manifest, and by the scriptures of the prophets* (Romans 16:26). What Yahusha (Jesus) says only in parables is that same hidden thing, and it was never apart from the prophets.
cards.member_note: Romans 16:25 — *according to the revelation of the mystery, which was kept secret since the world began.* Paul says the mystery kept secret since the world began is now made manifest through the scriptures of the prophets.

cards.src_text: Then Yahusha (Jesus) sent the multitude away, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field.
cards.tgt_text: Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.
cards.old_note: *Ye are of your father the devil* — the children-of-the-wicked-one substance.
cards.note: John 8:44 — *Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.* *Then Yahusha (Jesus) sent the multitude away, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field.* (Matthew 13:36) They ask him to declare the parable, and he says who the tares are. In John he says it plainly to men standing in front of him: their father is the devil. A tare has a father just as the wheat has one, and the explanation in the house turns on that.
cards.prose: They ask him to declare the parable, and he says who the tares are. In John he says it plainly to men standing in front of him: their father is the devil. A tare has a father just as the wheat has one, and the explanation in the house turns on that.
cards.member_note: John 8:44 — *Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do.* He tells the men before him their father is the devil, a murderer from the beginning, the plain form of the tares' explanation.

cards.src_text: Then Yahusha (Jesus) sent the multitude away, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field.
cards.tgt_text: Whoever goes on sinning belongs to the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the very beginning. This is why the Son of Elohim (God) was revealed: to undo the works of the devil.
cards.old_note: The children-of-Elohim (God) vs the children-of-the-devil manifest by their fruit.
cards.note: 1 John 3:8 — *Whoever goes on sinning belongs to the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the very beginning. This is why the Son of Elohim (God) was revealed: to undo the works of the devil.* *Then Yahusha (Jesus) sent the multitude away, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field.* (Matthew 13:36) The disciples ask for the tares to be explained, and John gives the line that sorts them: *In this the children of Elohim (God) are manifest, and the children of the devil* (1 John 3:10). Fruit shows which are which. And the Son of Elohim (God) came to put an end to the devil's works, so the field is not left to him.
cards.prose: The disciples ask for the tares to be explained, and John gives the line that sorts them: *In this the children of Elohim (God) are manifest, and the children of the devil* (1 John 3:10). Fruit shows which are which. And the Son of Elohim (God) came to put an end to the devil's works, so the field is not left to him.
cards.member_note: 1 John 3:8 — *Whoever goes on sinning belongs to the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the very beginning. This is why the Son of Elohim (God) was revealed: to undo the works of the devil.* Children of Elohim (God) and children of the devil are made manifest, and the Son of Elohim (God) came to undo the devil's works.

cards.src_text: Then Yahusha (Jesus) sent the multitude away, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field.
cards.tgt_text: And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.
cards.old_note: The righteous-shining-as-the-sun substance.
cards.note: Daniel 12:3 — *And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.* *Then Yahusha (Jesus) sent the multitude away, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field.* (Matthew 13:36) The explanation of the tares ends with the righteous shining like the sun, and Daniel has the picture first: *shall shine as the brightness of the firmament*. The meaning of the tares ends in a shining that was already promised to the wise and to those who turn many to righteousness.
cards.prose: The explanation of the tares ends with the righteous shining like the sun, and Daniel has the picture first: *shall shine as the brightness of the firmament*. The meaning of the tares ends in a shining that was already promised to the wise and to those who turn many to righteousness.
cards.member_note: Daniel 12:3 — *they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament.* Daniel says the wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament and those who turn many to righteousness as the stars.

cards.src_text: Then Yahusha (Jesus) sent the multitude away, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field.
cards.tgt_text: Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:
cards.old_note: The kingdom-prepared-from-the-foundation-of-the-world.
cards.note: Matthew 25:34 — *Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:* *Then Yahusha (Jesus) sent the multitude away, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field.* (Matthew 13:36) Declare the parable, they asked, and the end of his answer is a kingdom for the righteous. The King says the same later to the sheep on his right hand, *prepared for you from the foundation of the world*. The wheat does not earn that place at the end. It was made ready long before the field was sown.
cards.prose: Declare the parable, they asked, and the end of his answer is a kingdom for the righteous. The King says the same later to the sheep on his right hand, *prepared for you from the foundation of the world*. The wheat does not earn that place at the end. It was made ready long before the field was sown.
cards.member_note: Matthew 25:34 — *Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:* The King calls the blessed to inherit a kingdom prepared for them from the foundation of the world.

cards.src_text: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man has found, he hides, and for joy thereof goes and selleth all that he has, and buyeth that field.
cards.tgt_text: Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee: therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.
cards.old_note: *Therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life* — the Father's-paying-the-price for the elect-treasure.
cards.note: Isaiah 43:4 — *Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee: therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.* *Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man has found, he hides, and for joy thereof goes and selleth all that he has, and buyeth that field.* (Matthew 13:44) The man who finds the treasure sells all he has to buy the field. Isaiah shows who pays for Yashar'el (Israel). Yahuah (the LORD) says *Since thou wast precious in my sight*, and so he will give men and peoples for the life of his own. The treasure is what he already counted precious.
cards.prose: The man who finds the treasure sells all he has to buy the field. Isaiah shows who pays for Yashar'el (Israel). Yahuah (the LORD) says *Since thou wast precious in my sight*, and so he will give men and peoples for the life of his own. The treasure is what he already counted precious.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 43:4 — *Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee: therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.* Because Yashar'el (Israel) was precious in his sight, Yahuah (the LORD) gives men and peoples for its life.

cards.src_text: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man has found, he hides, and for joy thereof goes and selleth all that he has, and buyeth that field.
cards.tgt_text: Who, being in the form of Elohim (God), thought it not robbery to be equal with Elohim (God):
cards.old_note: *Made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant* — the King's-paying-the-price.
cards.note: Philippians 2:6 — *Who, being in the form of Elohim (God), thought it not robbery to be equal with Elohim (God):* *Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man has found, he hides, and for joy thereof goes and selleth all that he has, and buyeth that field.* (Matthew 13:44) The man gives up all he has to get the field. Paul writes of one who, being in the form of Elohim (God), *made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant* (Philippians 2:7). He let go of what was his in order to take what he came for.
cards.prose: The man gives up all he has to get the field. Paul writes of one who, being in the form of Elohim (God), *made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant* (Philippians 2:7). He let go of what was his in order to take what he came for.
cards.member_note: Philippians 2:6 — *Who, being in the form of Elohim (God), thought it not robbery to be equal with Elohim (God):* He who was in the form of Elohim (God) gave up what was his and took the form of a servant.

cards.src_text: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man has found, he hides, and for joy thereof goes and selleth all that he has, and buyeth that field.
cards.tgt_text: For thou art an holy people unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.
cards.old_note: *Yahuah (the LORD) thy Elohim (God) hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth* — the treasure-people Tanakh-substance.
cards.note: Deuteronomy 7:6 — *For thou art an holy people unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.* *Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man has found, he hides, and for joy thereof goes and selleth all that he has, and buyeth that field.* (Matthew 13:44) The treasure is hid in a field and bought with everything the man has. Moses tells what Yahuah (the LORD) calls his own treasure, a holy people chosen *to be a special people unto himself*. It was not their number that moved him, since *ye were the fewest of all people* (Deuteronomy 7:7).
cards.prose: The treasure is hid in a field and bought with everything the man has. Moses tells what Yahuah (the LORD) calls his own treasure, a holy people chosen *to be a special people unto himself*. It was not their number that moved him, since *ye were the fewest of all people* (Deuteronomy 7:7).
cards.member_note: Deuteronomy 7:6 — *Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.* Yahuah (the LORD) has chosen a holy people to be a special people to himself, above all peoples on the earth.

cards.src_text: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind:
cards.tgt_text: When the Son of Adam shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory:
cards.old_note: *When the Son of Adam shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory:* (Matthew 25:31). The net *gathered of every kind*, and the good were gathered into vessels while the bad were cast away (Matthew 13:47-48). The shepherd's dividing is the same sorting of the gathered: the seed brought out of all nations, then sifted, the sheep from the goats.
cards.note: Matthew 25:31 — *When the Son of Adam shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory:* *Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind:* (Matthew 13:47) The net gathers *of every kind*, and the sorting happens at the shore. The Son of Adam on his throne does the same with sheep and goats: everything brought before him is divided, one from another. The gathering comes first and the dividing second, and the dividing is his work, not the fishermen's.
cards.prose: The net gathers *of every kind*, and the sorting happens at the shore. The Son of Adam on his throne does the same with sheep and goats: everything brought before him is divided, one from another. The gathering comes first and the dividing second, and the dividing is his work, not the fishermen's.
cards.member_note: Matthew 25:31 — *When the Son of Adam shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory:* The Son of Adam sits on his throne of glory to divide the gathered, as the net is sorted at the shore.

Daniel shows two outcomes in the graves as well. Of the many who sleep in the dust, some wake *to everlasting life* and some *to shame and everlasting contempt*. The men of Anathoth, his own townsmen, told him *Prophesy not in the name of Yahuah (LORD)* and sought his life. It is an old pattern. The word comes to its own house and the house will not have it.

threads.title: Let the dead bury their dead, and the fifth commandment
threads.summary_md:
*It ain't new.* The man asks for what the fathers did, and the commandment he stands on was written long before him. One of the disciples says:

*And another of his disciples said unto him, Adonai (Lord), suffer me first to go and bury my father.* (Matthew 8:21)

*But Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead.* (Matthew 8:22)

Read as a word against honouring a father, that answer would put Yahusha (Jesus) at odds with Moses, in the same Matthew where he has just said he did not come to destroy the law. The commandment is plain:

*Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee.* (Exodus 20:12)

The fathers did exactly what this disciple asks. Joseph stood before Pharaoh with the same request:

*My father made me swear, saying, Lo, I die: in my grave which I have digged for me in the land of Canaan, there shalt thou bury me. Now therefore let me go up, I pray thee, and bury my father, and I will come again.* (Genesis 50:5)

And when Yahusha (Jesus) is speaking of this very commandment in Mark, he does not loosen it. He defends it against the elders who had found a way around it:

*For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:* (Mark 7:10)

*Making the word of Elohim (God) of none effect through your tradition, which ye have delivered: and many such like things do ye.* (Mark 7:13)

Whatever he means by the dead burying their dead, the man who says it in Matthew is the man who guards the fifth commandment in Mark, so it cannot be a teaching against honouring a father. What the saying does show is the weight of the call. *Follow me* stands first in the sentence, and the cost is the one he has just named to the scribe, a Son of Adam with nowhere to lay his head.

threads.title: The twelve he calls, and the twelve tribes they are set over
threads.summary_md:
Matthew counts his men before he sends them. They are twelve, called to him and given power.

*And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.* (Matthew 10:1)

The number matches something. Yahusha (Jesus) tells these same men what it is for, once on the road and once at the table.

*Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 19:28)

*That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Luke 22:30)

Twelve men for twelve tribes. That is why the errand is to the lost sheep of those same tribes, wherever they have been scattered.

*But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 10:6)

The count is kept to the end of the story. The people sealed in Revelation are counted by tribe, and the city has the tribes on its gates and the apostles in its foundations.

*And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Revelation 7:4)

*And had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel):* (Revelation 21:12)

*And the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.* (Revelation 21:14)

The choosing was his before the sending was. Mark shows him going up the mountain and picking them himself, and Luke shows him spending the night in prayer first.

*And he goeth up into a mountain, and calleth unto him whom he would: and they came unto him.* (Mark 3:13)

So the twelve are men he chose, for a people he named, to judge a people he is gathering, and the city at the end carries both sets of names.

threads.title: Heal the sick, and give freely what was freely given
threads.summary_md:
*It ain't new.* The works Yahusha (Jesus) puts in the hands of the twelve were written down by Isaiah as the signs of the day Elohim (God) comes to save.

*Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely ye have received, freely give.* (Matthew 10:8)

Isaiah spoke to people with fearful hearts and told them who was coming.

*Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your Elohim (God) will come with vengeance, even Elohim (God) with a recompence; he will come and save you.* (Isaiah 35:4)

*Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.* (Isaiah 35:5)

Yahusha (Jesus) reads from the same list when John sends to ask whether he is the one who should come.

*The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.* (Matthew 11:5)

So when the twelve heal, they are not doing something new. They carry the sign the prophet gave, and the sign points back to the one who sent them.

The gift also goes out the way it came in. Nobody paid for it, so nobody is to be charged for it. Simon saw the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) given and tried to buy his way in.

*And when Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles’ hands the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) was given, he offered them money,* (Acts 8:18)

The words in Matthew leave no room for that. What was received freely is given freely.

threads.title: Shake off the dust, and the day Sodom is measured against
threads.summary_md:
The twelve are told what to do with a town that will not have them.

*And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.* (Matthew 10:14)

It is the same teaching he gave the crowd, now with the men who must live it.

*Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.* (Matthew 7:6)

He had shown them how it is done. A whole city saw him and sent him away, and he went.

*And, behold, the whole city came out to meet Yahusha (Jesus): and when they saw him, they besought him that he would depart out of their coasts.* (Matthew 8:34)

The twelve do not follow after a hearing that is refused, and they do not stay to fight over it. Paul and Barnabas do the same, and the verse ends with them on the road to the next city.

*But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came unto Iconium.* (Acts 13:51)

The sending is broad because the sheep are scattered, and the dust is shaken only where the word has been heard and turned away. Then comes the weight of it. He sets a refused town against Sodom.

*Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.* (Matthew 10:15)

Sodom's end is written plainly.

*Then Yahuah (LORD) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Yahuah (LORD) out of heaven;* (Genesis 19:24)

He says the same over Capernaum.

*And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.* (Matthew 11:23)

A town that has been shown the works and the word answers for more than the one that burned. The measure is how much was shown.

threads.title: Until the Son of Adam be come
threads.summary_md:
*It ain't new.* The coming that Yahusha (Jesus) sets as the limit of the twelve's going was in Daniel before he ever spoke of it.

*But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel), till the Son of Adam be come.* (Matthew 10:23)

*I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.* (Daniel 7:13)

Daniel keeps the word like, one like the Son of Adam, and that fits the one who took on flesh and came to resemble the sons of Adam. Yahusha (Jesus) takes the name from the vision and uses it for himself. Then he says what the coming looks like.

*And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.* (Matthew 24:30)

*For the Son of Adam shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.* (Matthew 16:27)

So the going over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel) is not an errand that ends in a season. It is a standing errand, carried from city to city while the scattered are gathered, and it runs until the day he is seen coming with power. On that day the reward follows the works.
