members.member_note: Luke 17:14 — *And when he saw them, he said unto them, Go shew yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed.* Ten lepers are sent to the priests as Moses laid down and are cleansed on the way, the same road the healed man in Matthew takes.

Matthew 5:17 — *Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.* He says plainly that he has not come to destroy the law or the prophets, which the sending of the leper to the priest bears out.

Matthew 12:9 — *And when he was departed thence, he went into their synagogue:* He enters the synagogue where the man with the withered hand is waiting, and what follows is the Torah kept against the rules laid over it.

Mark 7:10 — *For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:* Moses said to honour father and mother, and Yahusha (Jesus) holds to that commandment against the tradition that emptied it.

Acts 6:7 — *And the word of Elohim (God) increased; and the number of the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem greatly; and a great company of the priests were obedient to the faith.* A great company of the priests become obedient in Jerusalem, so the testimony the cleansed were sent to give the priesthood was heard.

Leviticus 13:45 — *And the leper in whom the plague is, his clothes shall be rent, and his head bare, and he shall put a covering upon his upper lip, and shall cry, Unclean, unclean.* This shows the place the Torah gave the leper, outside and crying unclean, which the touch of Yahusha (Jesus) lifts.

Luke 17:11 — *And it came to pass, as he went to Jerusalem, that he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.* Luke sets the road through Samaria and Galilee where ten lepers meet him and are sent to the priests, the same procedure as in Matthew.

Luke 7:1 — *Now when he had ended all his sayings in the audience of the people, he entered into Capernaum.* Luke brings him into Capernaum and tells that the centurion first sent elders of the Yahudim (Jews) to ask on his behalf.

Jeremiah 31:8 — *I will bring them from the north country, and gather them from the coasts of the earth.* The great company brought back from the north country and the coasts of the earth is the scattered house of Yashar'el (Israel) coming home.

Romans 11:25 — *that blindness in part is happened to Yashar'el (Israel), until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.* The fulness of the Gentiles coming in is the scattered seed of Yashar'el (Israel) gathered home, the many who sit down with the fathers.

Isaiah 35:5 — *Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.* Isaiah's picture of the day Elohim (God) comes to save, with the eyes of the blind opened, is what these healings show.

Matthew 11:4 — *Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said unto them, Go and shew John again those things which ye do hear and see:* Yahusha (Jesus) answers John in prison by pointing to the same healings Matthew has just shown, as his own credential.

Psalm 8:4 — *What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of Adam, that thou visitest him?* David asks what the son of Adam is that Elohim (God) should visit him, and in Matthew the visit has come.

Luke 3:38 — *which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of Elohim (God).* Luke's genealogy runs back to Adam, the son of Elohim (God), the lineage the title Son of Adam carries.

Exodus 20:12 — *Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee.* The fifth commandment is the Torah ground under the disciple's request, and the answer he is given does not remove it.

Genesis 50:5 — *My father made me swear, saying, Lo, I die: in my grave which I have digged for me in the land of Canaan, there shalt thou bury me. Now therefore let me go up, I pray thee, and bury my father, and I will come again.* Joseph asks leave to go up and bury his father and is granted it, the pattern of the fathers behind the disciple's request.

Mark 7:10 — *For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:* Moses said to honour father and mother, and Yahusha (Jesus) defends that commandment against the tradition that emptied it.

Psalm 89:8 — *O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of hosts, who is a strong Yahuah (LORD) like unto thee? or to thy faithfulness round about thee?* The psalm asks who is like Yahuah (the LORD) and answers that he rules the raging of the sea, which the disciples see at the boat.

Psalm 107:23 — *They that go down to the sea in ships, that do business in great waters;* Men who go down to the sea in ships see the works of Yahuah (the LORD) in the deep, the same sight the disciples have in the storm.

Job 38:8 — *Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth, as if it had issued out of the womb?* Job is asked who shut up the sea with doors and said how far it may come, the authority shown in the boat.

Jonah 1:5 — *But Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.* Jonah sleeps in a ship in a storm sent after him, while Yahusha (Jesus) sleeps in peace and stills the storm himself.

Matthew 12:41 — *because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.* Yahusha (Jesus) says a greater than Jonas is here, which the stilled sea in the boat had already shown the disciples.

1 John 3:8 — *This is why the Son of Elohim (God) was revealed: to undo the works of the devil.* The Son of Elohim (God) was revealed to undo the works of the devil, which the spirits in the tombs seem to know at once.

2 Peter 2:4 — *cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment.* Elohim (God) did not spare the angels that sinned but kept them for judgment, the appointed time the spirits fear in Matthew.

Jude 1:6 — *he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.* The angels who left their first estate are reserved for the judgment of the great day, the day the spirits fear in Matthew.

Leviticus 11:7 — *And the swine, though he divide the hoof, and be clovenfooted, yet he cheweth not the cud; he is unclean to you.* Moses names the swine as unclean, so the herd beside the tombs is a plain sign of defilement and of a place living away from the Torah.

Deuteronomy 14:8 — *ye shall not eat of their flesh, nor touch their dead carcase.* A second witness in the Torah that the swine are unclean, adding that even their dead carcase was not to be touched.

Matthew 12:7 — *But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.* Yahusha (Jesus) hands the same words from Hosea to the Pharisees again, saying that knowing them would have kept them from condemning men who broke no commandment.

Psalm 40:6 — *Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required.* David says sacrifice and offering were not what Yahuah (the LORD) desired, and that he wanted an opened ear and the law kept within the heart.

Psalm 51:16 — *For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering.* David says he would give the sacrifice if it were wanted, and that what Elohim (God) will not despise is a broken and contrite heart.

Isaiah 1:11 — *I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats.* Yahuah (the LORD) asks what purpose a multitude of sacrifices serves when he is already full of them and takes no delight in the blood.

Jeremiah 7:21 — *Thus saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel); Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh.* Yahuah (the LORD) tells the people to pile offering on offering and eat the meat, since obeying his voice was what he asked first.

Amos 5:21 — *I hate, I despise your feast days, and I will not smell in your solemn assemblies.* Yahuah (the LORD) says he hates and despises feast days kept without justice, and asks for judgment to run down like water.

Micah 6:6 — *shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves of a year old?* A worshipper asks whether burnt offerings and year-old calves are how to come before Yahuah (the LORD), and the answer a few verses on is justice, mercy and a humble walk.

Hosea 2:19 — *And I will betroth thee unto me for ever; yea, I will betroth thee unto me in righteousness, and in judgment, and in lovingkindness, and in mercies.* Yahuah (the LORD) promises to betroth the scattered house to himself for ever, in righteousness, judgment, lovingkindness and mercies, which is the wedding the bridegroom speaks of.

Isaiah 54:5 — *For thy Maker is thine husband; Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel); The Elohim (God) of the whole earth shall he be called.* Yahuah (the LORD) is named as the husband of the forsaken woman, and he will gather her with great mercies.

Jeremiah 3:14 — *for I am married unto you: and I will take you one of a city, and two of a family, and I will bring you to Zion.* Yahuah (the LORD) tells backsliding children he is married to them and will bring them to Zion, taking them one from a city and two from a family.

John 3:29 — *the friend of the bridegroom, which standeth and heareth him, rejoiceth greatly.* John calls himself the friend of the bridegroom who rejoices at the bridegroom's voice, and so names whose wedding it is.

Ephesians 5:25 — *Husbands, love your wives, even as Messiah (Christ) also loved the church, and gave himself for it;* Paul sets the bridegroom's own love in the household, the husband giving himself for the one he loves.

Revelation 19:7 — *Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready.* The marriage of the Lamb has come and his wife is ready, so the time of fasting ends in the feast.

Revelation 21:2 — *And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from Elohim (God) out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.* John sees the holy city coming down from Elohim (God) prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.

Isaiah 11:1 — *And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots:* Isaiah has a rod come out of the stem of Jesse and a Branch grow from his roots, which is where the title Son of David comes from.

Jeremiah 23:5 — *Behold, the days come, saith Yahuah (LORD), that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.* Yahuah (the LORD) promises to raise a righteous Branch to David, a king who brings both Yahudah (Judah) and Yashar'el (Israel) safe.

Ezekiel 34:23 — *And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David.* Yahuah (the LORD) will set up one shepherd, his servant David, over the flock that was pushed about and scattered.

Ezekiel 37:24 — *And David my servant shall be king over them; and they all shall have one shepherd: they shall also walk in my judgments, and observe my statutes, and do them.* David my servant is king over the two houses made one, and they walk in Yahuah's (the LORD's) judgments and statutes and do them.

Matthew 15:22 — *a woman of Canaan came out of the same coasts, and cried unto him.* A woman from the coast of Tyre and Sidon cries out to Yahusha (Jesus) in the same words, Son of David, have mercy on me.

Matthew 20:30 — *And, behold, two blind men sitting by the way side, when they heard that Yahusha (Jesus) passed by, cried out, saying, Have mercy on us, O Adonai (Lord), thou Son of David.* Two blind men cry the same words on the road out of Jericho, and when the crowd hushes them they only cry louder.

Matthew 21:9 — *Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of Yahuah (Lord).* The crowds on the road into Jerusalem cry Hosanna to the Son of David and say he comes in the name of Yahuah (the Lord).

Daniel 7:13 — *I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days.* Daniel sees one like the Son of Adam brought to the Ancient of days and given everlasting dominion, the authority behind the claim at the bed.

Matthew 28:18 — *And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* At the end of Matthew he says all power in heaven and earth is given to him, the whole of what he showed at the bed.
Luke 19:10 — *For the Son of Adam is come to seek and to save that which was lost.* The Son of Adam says he came to seek and to save the lost, the same errand he gave at Matthew's table.

Ezekiel 36:26 — *A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you.* Yahuah (the LORD) promises a new heart and a new spirit within, the vessel that can hold the commandments kept from the inside.

Matthew 5:17 — *Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.* Yahusha (Jesus) says he has not come to destroy the law or the prophets, so the new wine is not a new law.

Leviticus 15:25 — *all the days of the issue of her uncleanness shall be as the days of her separation: she shall be unclean.* The Torah's rule on an issue of blood that runs long, which kept the woman unclean for the twelve years she bled.

Matthew 8:2 — *And, behold, there came a leper and worshipped him, saying, Adonai (Lord), if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.* A leper tells Yahusha (Jesus) that if he is willing he can make him clean, another unclean man who comes to him.
Daniel 12:2 — *many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake.* Daniel says many who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, the word Yahusha (Jesus) uses of the ruler's daughter.

Isaiah 26:19 — *Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust: for thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead.* Isaiah tells those who dwell in dust to awake and sing, and says the earth shall cast out the dead.

John 11:11 — *Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep.* Yahusha (Jesus) says his friend Lazarus sleepeth and he goes to wake him, using the word he used for the ruler's daughter.

1 Thessalonians 4:13 — *concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope.* Paul will not have the brethren ignorant about those who are asleep, so that they do not sorrow as people without hope.

Matthew 12:22 — *he healed him, insomuch that the blind and dumb both spake and saw.* A man both blind and dumb is healed so that he speaks and sees, and the same charge about the prince of the devils follows.

Matthew 12:31 — *but the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) shall not be forgiven unto men.* He says every sin and blasphemy can be forgiven except blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), after his works were called the prince of devils' doing.

2 Kings 1:2 — *enquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron whether I shall recover of this disease.* A king of Samaria sends to Baal-zebub the god of Ekron to ask whether he will recover, the name behind the charge of the prince of the devils.

Zechariah 10:2 — *therefore they went their way as a flock, they were troubled, because there was no shepherd.* Zechariah says the people went their way as a flock, troubled because there was no shepherd, after idols and diviners comforted in vain.
John 4:35 — *Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest.* He tells his disciples the fields are already white to harvest, the same harvest he calls plenteous.

Matthew 10:1 — *he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.* He calls the twelve and gives them power over unclean spirits and every sickness, the answer to his request for labourers.

Matthew 19:28 — *ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* Yahusha (Jesus) promises the men who followed him twelve thrones over the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel), which is why there are twelve of them.

Luke 22:30 — *That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* At the last supper he promises the same men a place at his table in the kingdom and thrones over the twelve tribes.

Revelation 21:14 — *And the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.* The names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb are set in the twelve foundations of the city wall.

Revelation 21:12 — *names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* The twelve gates of the city carry the names of the twelve tribes, the same tribes the twelve are sent to.

Revelation 7:4 — *sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* A hundred and forty-four thousand are sealed from all the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), counted by tribe.

Ezekiel 47:1 — *waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward.* Ezekiel sees water running out from under the threshold of the restored house, the place the gathered tribes are brought to.
Matthew 7:6 — *neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet.* On the mountain he teaches that what is holy is not pressed on those who trample it.
Matthew 8:34 — *they besought him that he would depart out of their coasts.* A whole city asks him to leave its coasts, and he leaves, which is the pattern for the twelve.
Acts 13:51 — *But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came unto Iconium.* Paul and Barnabas shake off the dust against a city and go on to Iconium.
Acts 18:6 — *I am clean: from henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles.* At Corinth Paul shakes out his raiment when the synagogue blasphemes, and turns to the Gentiles.

Genesis 19:24 — *Then Yahuah (LORD) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Yahuah (LORD) out of heaven;* Sodom's end, fire and brimstone from Yahuah (the LORD) out of heaven, is the measure he sets against the town that refuses.

Mark 3:13 — *And he goeth up into a mountain, and calleth unto him whom he would: and they came unto him.* Mark shows him going up a mountain and calling the twelve to himself, whom he would, and they came.
Luke 6:12 — *went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to Elohim (God).* Luke has him pray all night on the mountain before he chooses the twelve.

Acts 1:13 — *and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.* After the resurrection eleven of the men are named in the upper room, with the place of the one who betrayed him empty.

Matthew 15:24 — *But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* He tells the woman of Canaan the same scope he gave the twelve, the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).

Romans 1:16 — *to every one that believeth; to the Yahudi (Jew) first, and also to the Greek.* Paul keeps the order of the sending, the Yahudi (Jew) first and then the Greek, the house in the land and then the scattered house abroad.

Romans 15:8 — *was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of Elohim (God), to confirm the promises made unto the fathers.* Paul says Yahusha (Jesus) was a minister of the circumcision to confirm the promises made to the fathers.

Isaiah 35:5 — *Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.* Isaiah foretells the eyes of the blind opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped when Elohim (God) comes to save.

Matthew 11:5 — *the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.* Yahusha (Jesus) answers John's question with the same works he has just given the twelve power to do.

Acts 8:18 — *And when Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles’ hands the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) was given, he offered them money,* Simon offers money for the gift of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), the one thing the twelve were told to give freely.
Mark 6:11 — *shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them.* Mark gives the same instruction and names what the dust is for, a testimony against that town, with Sodom set beside it.
Luke 9:5 — *shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.* Luke has the same instruction, with the dust shaken off as they leave the city, for a testimony against it.

Matthew 11:23 — *if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.* Capernaum is told it will answer for more than Sodom, because Sodom never saw the works done there.
Genesis 8:11 — *in her mouth was an olive leaf pluckt off: so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.* A dove brings Noah an olive leaf and the news that the waters are going down.
Matthew 3:16 — *he saw the Spirit of Elohim (God) descending like a dove, and lighting upon him.* The Spirit of Elohim (God) comes down on Yahusha (Jesus) like a dove at his baptism.
Matthew 24:13 — *But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.* The same promise is spoken again in his words on the last days: the one who endures to the end is saved.

Mark 13:13 — *And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.* Mark pairs being hated for his name with the one who endures to the end being saved.

Hebrews 3:14 — *For we are made partakers of Messiah (Christ), if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end;* Hebrews says we share in Messiah (Christ) if we hold our first confidence steadfast to the end.

Hebrews 10:36 — *For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of Elohim (God), ye might receive the promise.* Hebrews says patience is needed so that, after the will of Elohim (God) is done, the promise is received.
Daniel 7:13 — *one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days.* Daniel sees one like the Son of Adam come with the clouds of heaven to the Ancient of days.

Matthew 24:30 — *they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.* The Son of Adam is seen coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory, and the tribes of the earth mourn.
Matthew 16:27 — *the Son of Adam shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels.* The Son of Adam comes in his Father's glory with his angels and rewards every man according to his works.
Isaiah 66:24 — *their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched.* Isaiah ends on the dead bodies of the transgressors, with the worm and the fire that do not stop.

Jeremiah 7:31 — *built the high places of Tophet, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire.* Jeremiah names Tophet in the valley of Hinnom, where sons and daughters were burned in the fire.

2 Kings 23:10 — *he defiled Topheth, which is in the valley of the children of Hinnom.* Josiah defiles Topheth in the valley of Hinnom so that no one can pass his son or daughter through the fire to Molech.
Revelation 20:14 — *And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.* Death and hell are cast into the lake of fire, and John calls it the second death.

Proverbs 9:10 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.* The fear of Yahuah (the LORD) is the beginning of wisdom, and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.

Luke 12:8 — *Also I say unto you, Whosoever shall confess me before men, him shall the Son of Adam also confess before the angels of Elohim (God):* Luke says whoever confesses him before men, the Son of Adam will confess before the angels of Elohim (God).
2 Timothy 2:12 — *If we suffer, we shall also reign with him: if we deny him, he also will deny us:* Paul says that if we suffer we reign with him, and if we deny him he will deny us.
Matthew 7:21 — *but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.* Saying Adonai (Lord) is not enough; the one who enters the kingdom is the one who does the Father's will.
Micah 7:6 — *a man’s enemies are the men of his own house.* Micah says a man's enemies are the men of his own house, the words Yahusha (Jesus) takes up.
Luke 12:51 — *Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division:* Luke records him saying he did not come to give peace on earth but division.

Genesis 3:15 — *between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.* Yahuah (the LORD) puts enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed, the first division.

Exodus 20:12 — *Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee.* The fifth commandment stands: honour thy father and thy mother, and the promise of long days on the land goes with it.
Matthew 16:24 — *let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.* After Peter's confession he tells his disciples to deny themselves, take up the cross, and follow.
Mark 8:34 — *let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.* Mark has him call the crowd in with his disciples to hear that anyone who follows must take up his cross.
Luke 9:23 — *let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.* Luke adds that the cross is taken up daily, and says it to them all.
Luke 14:27 — *And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.* Luke says the one who does not bear his cross and come after him cannot be his disciple.

Matthew 6:19 — *Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:* He tells the crowd not to lay up treasures on earth where moth and rust corrupt and thieves steal.
Psalm 49:1 — *Hear this, all ye people; give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world:* The psalm opens by calling every person in the world to listen before it speaks of wisdom.

John 13:20 — *Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that receiveth whomsoever I send receiveth me; and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.* John records the same chain: whoever receives the one he sends receives him, and whoever receives him receives the one who sent him.
Matthew 25:40 — *Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.* What is done to one of the least of his brethren he counts as done to himself.

Matthew 6:1 — *to be seen of them: otherwise ye have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.* Alms given before men to be seen have no reward from the Father, the opposite of the cup of water given quietly.

Matthew 25:34 — *Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.* At the judgment the King calls the sheep blessed and gives them the kingdom prepared from the foundation of the world.

Jeremiah 6:16 — *ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls.* Yahuah (the LORD) sets the rest at the end of a walk on the old paths, the good way, and records that the people refused it.

Isaiah 28:12 — *To whom he said, This is the rest wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest; and this is the refreshing: yet they would not hear.* Isaiah names the rest that eases the weary and says plainly that the people would not hear it.

Matthew 23:4 — *they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders.* Yahusha (Jesus) names the heavy, grievous load that was bound on the people's shoulders, the weight the weary are called out from.

Acts 15:10 — *to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear.* Peter names a yoke on the disciples' necks that neither the fathers nor he could bear, the kind of load Yahusha's (Jesus's) call to the weary lifts off.

Galatians 1:14 — *being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers.* Paul names the handed-down traditions he was once zealous for, the human weight laid over the commandments that the weary are called out from.

Jeremiah 31:33 — *I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts.* The covenant promise to the house of Yashar'el (Israel) is the law written in the heart, not set aside, and the rest he offers goes with it.

Ezekiel 36:26 — *I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.* Yahuah (the LORD) promises to take out the stony heart and give a heart of flesh, which is what makes his way light to carry.

1 John 5:3 — *For this is the love of Elohim (God), that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.* John says plainly that keeping the commandments is the love of Elohim (God) and that they are not grievous.

Matthew 5:17 — *Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.* Yahusha (Jesus) says he did not come to destroy the law or the prophets, so the rest he gives is not a release from the Torah.

Matthew 28:18 — *And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* After the resurrection the Son says again that all power has been given to him, the same handing over by the Father.

John 1:18 — *No man hath seen Elohim (God) at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him.* No man has seen the Father, and the only begotten Son, who is in his bosom, is the one who has declared him.
John 5:19 — *The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do.* The Son does nothing of himself but what he sees the Father do, so what he reveals is the Father's own.

John 14:6 — *Yahusha (Jesus) saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.* The Son says no man comes to the Father except through him, the same sole access to the Father.
John 10:30 — *I and my Father are one.* Yahusha (Jesus) says he and the Father are one, the oneness of the Son who receives all things from the Father.

John 17:1 — *Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son, that thy Son also may glorify thee.* In prayer the Son speaks to the Father as Father, asking to be glorified so that he may glorify the Father in return.
1 Corinthians 8:6 — *one Elohim (God), the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him.* Paul names one Elohim (God), the Father, from whom are all things, and the Son through whom are all things.

Hebrews 1:1 — *Elohim (God), who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets,* The Father spoke to the fathers by the prophets and in these last days by his Son, who is the way he makes himself known.

Colossians 1:15 — *Who is the image of the invisible Elohim (God), the firstborn of every creature:* The Son is the image of the invisible Elohim (God), the one who can be seen where the Father cannot.

Luke 4:17 — *there was delivered unto him the book of the prophet Esaias.* At Nazareth he is handed the same Isaiah scroll whose works he now sends back to John, and he reads it only as far as the acceptable year.

Matthew 17:10 — *And his disciples asked him, saying, Why then say the scribes that Elias must first come?* The disciples ask why the scribes say Elias must first come, and the answer that follows names John as that Elias.

Ezekiel 28:1 — *The word of Yahuah (LORD) came again unto me, saying,* Ezekiel's word against the prince of Tyre opens here, so Tyre stands under judgment before Yahusha (Jesus) says it will fare better than Chorazin.

Isaiah 23:1 — *it is laid waste, so that there is no house, no entering in.* Isaiah's burden of Tyre pictures the city laid waste, the judgment already on Tyre that Yahusha (Jesus) says would have turned to repentance had it seen his works.

Genesis 19:24 — *Then Yahuah (LORD) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Yahuah (LORD) out of heaven;* Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed by brimstone and fire, and Yahusha (Jesus) says Capernaum stands worse than they did.

John 5:19 — *The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do.* The Son does nothing of himself but what he sees the Father do, so the revealing he thanks the Father for is the Father's work.
John 10:14 — *I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine.* The Son knows his sheep and is known of them, the same knowing the Father and Son share, given to those who are his.

1 Corinthians 1:18 — *For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of Elohim (God).* Paul says the word of the cross is foolishness to those who perish and the power of Elohim (God) to those being saved.

Exodus 33:20 — *And he said, Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live.* Moses is told no man sees the Father's face and lives, so the Father must be made known by the Son who is seen.
1 Samuel 21:1 — *Then came David to Nob to Ahimelech the priest.* David came to the priest at Nob in need and was given the hallowed bread, and the Scripture tells it without a word of blame.

Leviticus 24:8 — *Every sabbath he shall set it in order before Yahuah (LORD) continually, being taken from the children of Yashar'el (Israel) by an everlasting covenant.* The bread was set in order before Yahuah (the LORD) every sabbath by an everlasting covenant, so sabbath work was commanded in the Torah itself.

Genesis 2:3 — *blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it.* Elohim (God) blessed the seventh day and made it holy at creation, so the day Yahusha (Jesus) is master of was set apart before any man's rule.

Exodus 20:8 — *Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.* The commandment itself, the plain word to remember the sabbath day and keep it holy, which Yahusha (Jesus) stands behind and never sets down.

John 7:22 — *Moses therefore gave unto you circumcision; (not because it is of Moses, but of the fathers;) and ye on the sabbath day circumcise a man.* Yahusha (Jesus) answers the sabbath accusation from their own practice: a man is circumcised on the sabbath so the law of Moses is kept, and so a man may be made whole.

Isaiah 58:13 — *call the sabbath a delight, the holy of Yahuah (LORD), honourable.* Isaiah calls the sabbath a delight and holy to Yahuah (the LORD), the day on which doing well belongs and the Pharisees' fence does not.

Hebrews 4:9 — *There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of Elohim (God).* Hebrews says a rest still remains for the people of Elohim (God), so the day Yahusha (Jesus) walked through the corn is not left behind.

Acts 17:2 — *And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them, and three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures,* Paul kept going into the synagogue on the sabbath days and reasoning from the scriptures, so the apostles carried the day forward rather than dropping it.

Daniel 7:25 — *and think to change times and laws.* Daniel pictures one who thinks to change times and laws, so when the sabbath is set aside the changing is his work, and it is not the Son of Adam's.

Matthew 9:34 — *But the Pharisees said, He casteth out devils through the prince of the devils.* The first time the Pharisees said he casts out devils through the prince of the devils, which sets up the full answer he gives here.
Matthew 10:25 — *If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub.* He had warned the twelve that if the master of the house is called Beelzebub, those of his household will be called the same.

Mark 3:28 — *Verily I say unto you, All sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme:* Mark gives the same saying and tells its reason: they said he had an unclean spirit, and that is where the line falls.

Luke 12:10 — *but unto him that blasphemeth against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) it shall not be forgiven.* Luke sets the same saying beside confessing him before men, with a word against the Son of Adam forgiven and blasphemy against the Spirit not.

Hebrews 6:4 — *have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit).* Hebrews warns those who tasted the heavenly gift and shared in the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) and then fall away, a turning from what was plainly seen.

Hebrews 10:26 — *For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins,* Hebrews speaks of sinning wilfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth, which describes a knowing refusal and not a stumble.
1 John 5:16 — *There is a sin unto death: I do not say that he shall pray for it.* John also recognizes a sin unto death, a different kind from the sin of a brother who can still be prayed for.

1 Timothy 1:13 — *Who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: but I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.* Paul obtained mercy for blasphemy and persecution because he acted ignorantly in unbelief, which shows what the forgivable side of the line looks like.

Jonah 1:17 — *Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.* Jonah spent three days and three nights in the fish, the exact measure Yahusha (Jesus) names as the sign for this generation.

Matthew 27:62 — *Now the next day, that followed the day of the preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees came together unto Pilate,* The chief priests and Pharisees went to Pilate remembering that he said he would rise after three days, so the sign was known to the very men who asked for one.

Matthew 28:1 — *In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week.* The women come to the sepulchre at the end of the sabbath as the first day dawns, which is where the sign of the three days is answered.

Matthew 11:21 — *if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon.* Chorazin and Bethsaida saw the mighty works and did not repent, so Yahusha (Jesus) holds them to account the same way he holds this generation.

Matthew 7:21 — *but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.* At the end of the Sermon the one who does the will of his Father is the one who enters, the same test that names his family here.
Matthew 25:31 — *then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory.* The Son of Adam comes on the throne of his glory and calls those on his right hand blessed of his Father.
John 15:14 — *Ye are my friends, if ye do whatsoever I command you.* Yahusha (Jesus) calls those his friends who do whatsoever he commands, the same doing that makes a brother, sister and mother.

1 John 2:3 — *And hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments.* John says we know that we know him if we keep his commandments, the same measure of belonging Yahusha (Jesus) uses for his family.

John 19:26 — *When Yahusha (Jesus) therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son!* At the cross he sees his mother and gives her a home with the disciple, so the family he names by the Father's will never sets honour aside.

Mark 7:9 — *And he said unto them, Full well ye reject the commandment of Elohim (God), that ye may keep your own tradition.* Mark records him rebuking men who reject the commandment of Elohim (God) for their own tradition, using the example of leaving father and mother without help.

Isaiah 56:1 — *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD), Keep ye judgment, and do justice: for my salvation is near to come, and my righteousness to be revealed.* Isaiah joins keeping judgment and doing justice with keeping the sabbath from polluting it, so mercy and the sabbath are held in one breath.

Isaiah 11:2 — *the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might.* Isaiah sees the Spirit of Yahuah (the LORD) resting on the Branch from Jesse with wisdom, understanding, counsel and might, the anointing the servant carries.

Isaiah 61:1 — *hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek.* Isaiah has the one anointed by the Spirit sent to the meek, the brokenhearted and the bound, which is the work the servant is doing.

Matthew 4:17 — *From that time Yahusha (Jesus) began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.* At the start he preached that the kingdom of heaven was at hand, and casting out the devil is the sign that it has arrived.

Luke 11:20 — *But if I with the finger of Elohim (God) cast out devils, no doubt the kingdom of Elohim (God) is come upon you.* Luke says the finger of Elohim (God) where Matthew says the Spirit, the same power at work, and the kingdom has come upon them.

Daniel 2:44 — *shall the Elohim (God) of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed.* Daniel saw a kingdom raised up by heaven that would never be destroyed, the kingdom that has come upon them as the devil is cast out.

John 11:52 — *And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad.* John says Yahusha (Jesus) came to gather into one the children of Elohim (God) who were scattered abroad, the gathering he says some refuse to join.

Ezekiel 34:11 — *For thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out.* Yahuah (the LORD) promises to search out his scattered sheep and bring them home, so the gathering Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of is the Shepherd's own work.

1 Kings 10:1 — *she came to prove him with hard questions.* The queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame and came with hard questions, the witness Yahusha (Jesus) sets against a generation with a greater than Solomon before it.

Deuteronomy 18:15 — *will raise up unto thee a Prophet from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me.* Moses told Yashar'el (Israel) that Yahuah (the LORD) would raise up a Prophet from among their brethren, and to him they were to hearken.

Genesis 6:1 — *And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them,* Men multiply on the earth and daughters are born, the opening of the hour when the enemy's seed was sown among them.

Genesis 3:1 — *And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath Elohim (God) said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?* The serpent's first words to the woman put what Elohim (God) had said in doubt, the enemy sowing his seed in the garden.

John 8:44 — *Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do.* Yahusha (Jesus) names the father of men who would not hear him, the plain statement that some in the crowd are children of the wicked one.

1 John 3:8 — *Whoever goes on sinning belongs to the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the very beginning. This is why the Son of Elohim (God) was revealed: to undo the works of the devil.* John says the devil has worked from the beginning and the Son of Elohim (God) was revealed to undo his works.

1 Samuel 2:12 — *Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they knew not Yahuah (LORD).* Priest's sons born in the chosen line are called sons of Belial who knew not Yahuah (the LORD), a tare sown inside the house.

Ezekiel 20:33 — *surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out, will I rule over you.* Yahuah (the LORD) will rule over the scattered house with a mighty hand and bring it into the wilderness to be tried face to face.

Ezekiel 20:33 — *surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out, will I rule over you.* Yahuah (the LORD) declares he will rule over the house he scattered, the rule that clears the kingdom and gathers his people home.
Matthew 7:21 — *but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.* Lawlessness is the measure: only the one who does the will of the Father enters, whatever he calls the King.

Luke 3:17 — *Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and will gather the wheat into his garner; but the chaff he will burn with fire unquenchable.* John says the coming one clears his floor, keeps the wheat in his garner, and burns the chaff with unquenchable fire.

Matthew 25:34 — *Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:* The King welcomes the blessed to a kingdom prepared for them from the foundation of the world.

Zechariah 13:8 — *two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.* In all the land two parts are cut off and die and a third is left, so being born in the field is not enough.

Matthew 24:31 — *they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.* The Son of Adam sends his angels with a trumpet to gather his elect from the four winds.

Revelation 14:14 — *upon the cloud one sat like unto the Son of Adam, having on his head a golden crown, and in his hand a sharp sickle.* John sees the harvest of the earth: one like the Son of Adam on a white cloud with a crown and a sharp sickle.

Isaiah 6:9 — *And he said, Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.* Isaiah is sent to this people with the word to hear indeed and not understand, the commission Matthew says the parables fulfil.
John 10:26 — *But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep, as I said unto you.* Those who believe not are not of his sheep, the sheep being the ones who hear.

1 Corinthians 2:14 — *the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of Elohim (God): for they are foolishness unto him.* The natural man cannot receive the things of the Spirit of Elohim (God); they are foolishness to him and are spiritually discerned.
John 12:37 — *But though he had done so many miracles before them, yet they believed not on him:* Though he did so many miracles before them they believed not, and John answers it with Isaiah.

Acts 28:25 — *Well spake the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers.* Paul says the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) spoke the word about hearing without understanding through Isaiah to the fathers, as his hearers at Rome parted.
Romans 11:7 — *but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded.* Yashar'el (Israel) did not obtain what it sought; the election obtained it and the rest were blinded.

1 Peter 1:10 — *Of which salvation the prophets have enquired and searched diligently, who prophesied of the grace that should come unto you:* The prophets searched diligently into the salvation the disciples are now seeing.
Daniel 2:21 — *he giveth wisdom unto the wise, and knowledge to them that know understanding.* Elohim (God) is the one who gives wisdom and knowledge, which is why the mysteries are given to some.

Matthew 13:36 — *Then Yahusha (Jesus) sent the multitude away, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field.* The disciples ask for the parable of the tares to be declared, the explanation the net repeats in another picture.
Matthew 4:19 — *And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.* Yahusha (Jesus) calls the first disciples to follow him and become fishers of men, the work of the net.
Ezekiel 47:9 — *there shall be a very great multitude of fish, because these waters shall come thither.* Where the river's waters come the sea is healed and a great multitude of fish live in it.

Matthew 25:31 — *When the Son of Adam shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory:* The Son of Adam comes in glory with the holy angels to sit on his throne and divide the gathered.

Daniel 12:2 — *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* Many who sleep in the dust awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame and everlasting contempt.

Exodus 12:15 — *for whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Yashar'el (Israel).* Leaven is put out of the house at the feast and the one who eats it is cut off from Yashar'el (Israel).

Leviticus 2:11 — *No meat offering, which ye shall bring unto Yahuah (LORD), shall be made with leaven.* No meal offering brought to Yahuah (the LORD) may be made with leaven, so leaven in the meal is out of place.

Matthew 16:6 — *Then Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.* Yahusha (Jesus) tells the disciples to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the Sadducees.

Matthew 16:11 — *that I spake it not to you concerning bread, that ye should beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.* He was not speaking of bread but warning them against the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees, which the next verse calls their teaching.
Luke 12:1 — *Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.* Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples first of all to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
1 Corinthians 5:6 — *Your glorying is not good. Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump?* A little leaven leavens the whole lump, said to people whose glorying was not good.
Galatians 5:9 — *A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump.* A little leaven leavens the whole lump, said of the persuasion that was hindering the Galatians from obeying the truth.

Genesis 18:6 — *And Abraham hastened into the tent unto Sarah, and said, Make ready quickly three measures of fine meal, knead it, and make cakes upon the hearth.* Abraham has Sarah make ready three measures of fine meal the day Yahuah (the LORD) came to his tent, the quantity the woman's leaven is hid in.

Matthew 13:43 — *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.* He repeats the call to hear at the end of the tares' explanation, after the righteous shine in the kingdom of their Father.

Deuteronomy 29:4 — *Yet Yahuah (LORD) hath not given you an heart to perceive, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, unto this day.* Moses tells all Yashar'el (Israel) that Yahuah (the LORD) had not yet given them a heart to perceive, eyes to see, or ears to hear.

1 Corinthians 2:7 — *But we speak the wisdom of Elohim (God) in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom, which Elohim (God) ordained before the world unto our glory:* Paul speaks the hidden wisdom of Elohim (God) in a mystery, ordained before the world.
Ephesians 3:3 — *How that by revelation he made known unto me the mystery; (as I wrote afore in few words,* Paul says the mystery was made known to him by revelation, not by his own working.
John 12:37 — *But though he had done so many miracles before them, yet they believed not on him:* Though he had done so many miracles before them, they believed not on him.

Acts 28:25 — *Well spake the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers.* Paul at Rome says the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) spoke the word about seeing without perceiving by Isaiah to the fathers.
Romans 11:7 — *but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded.* The election obtained what Yashar'el (Israel) sought, and the rest were blinded.

Matthew 13:36 — *Then Yahusha (Jesus) sent the multitude away, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field.* The disciples ask him in the house to declare the parable of the tares, and he gives them the plain account.

Genesis 6:1 — *And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them,* Men multiplied on the earth and daughters were born, the field the good seed was sown in.

Genesis 3:1 — *And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath Elohim (God) said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?* The serpent asks the woman whether Elohim (God) really said it, the enemy's first move against the sown word.

Ezekiel 17:22 — *I will crop off from the top of his young twigs a tender one, and will plant it upon an high mountain and eminent.* Yahuah (the LORD) takes a tender twig and plants it on the high mountain of Yashar'el (Israel), where it becomes a great tree.

Daniel 4:12 — *the beasts of the field had shadow under it, and the fowls of the heaven dwelt in the boughs thereof, and all flesh was fed of it.* Nebuchadnezzar's great tree shelters the beasts and the fowls of heaven and feeds all flesh, the picture of a kingdom.

Ezekiel 31:6 — *All the fowls of heaven made their nests in his boughs, and under his branches did all the beasts of the field bring forth their young, and under his shadow dwelt all great nations.* Ezekiel's great tree has the fowls of heaven nesting in its boughs and great nations dwelling in its shadow.
Psalm 78:2 — *I will open my mouth in a parable: I will utter dark sayings of old:* The psalmist opens his mouth in a parable and utters dark sayings of old, the word Yahusha (Jesus) takes up.

Romans 16:25 — *according to the revelation of the mystery, which was kept secret since the world began.* Paul says the mystery kept secret since the world began is now made manifest through the scriptures of the prophets.

John 8:44 — *Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do.* He tells the men before him their father is the devil, a murderer from the beginning, the plain form of the tares' explanation.

1 John 3:8 — *Whoever goes on sinning belongs to the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the very beginning. This is why the Son of Elohim (God) was revealed: to undo the works of the devil.* Children of Elohim (God) and children of the devil are made manifest, and the Son of Elohim (God) came to undo the devil's works.

Daniel 12:3 — *they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament.* Daniel says the wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament and those who turn many to righteousness as the stars.

Matthew 25:34 — *Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:* The King calls the blessed to inherit a kingdom prepared for them from the foundation of the world.

Isaiah 43:4 — *Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee: therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.* Because Yashar'el (Israel) was precious in his sight, Yahuah (the LORD) gives men and peoples for its life.

Philippians 2:6 — *Who, being in the form of Elohim (God), thought it not robbery to be equal with Elohim (God):* He who was in the form of Elohim (God) gave up what was his and took the form of a servant.

Deuteronomy 7:6 — *Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.* Yahuah (the LORD) has chosen a holy people to be a special people to himself, above all peoples on the earth.

Matthew 25:31 — *When the Son of Adam shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory:* The Son of Adam sits on his throne of glory to divide the gathered, as the net is sorted at the shore.

Daniel 12:2 — *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* Many who sleep in the dust awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame and everlasting contempt.

Matthew 5:17 — *Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.* He did not come to destroy the law or the prophets but to fulfil them, so the old stays in the treasure.
Romans 7:22 — *For I delight in the law of Elohim (God) after the inward man:* Paul delights in the law of Elohim (God) after the inward man, the old held in the new heart.

Jeremiah 31:33 — *I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts.* In the new covenant with the house of Yashar'el (Israel) the same law is put in their inward parts and written on their hearts.
John 7:5 — *For neither did his brethren believe in him.* Even his brothers did not believe in him, the offence in his own house.
Mark 6:1 — *And he went out from thence, and came into his own country; and his disciples follow him.* Mark records the same return to his own country and the offence of those who knew his family.

Luke 4:16 — *he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read.* At Nazareth, where he was raised, he goes into the synagogue on the sabbath as his custom was and stands to read.

Jeremiah 11:21 — *thus saith Yahuah (LORD) of the men of Anathoth, that seek thy life, saying, Prophesy not in the name of Yahuah (LORD).* The men of Anathoth, Jeremiah's own townsmen, seek his life and tell him not to prophesy in the name of Yahuah (the LORD).
